name: Academic Resource Center
description: The ARC is committed to empowering students to reach their full academic potential in an inclusive and equitable academic environment. The ARC supports Harvard’s GSAS students in developing time management skills, study strategies, and metacognitive approaches to learning and welcomes graduate students to sign up for academic coaching, accountability groups, panel discussions, and workshops.

name: Active Minds Student Chapter at CAMHS
description: Active Minds @ Harvard/CAMHS, is a peer education group under the umbrella of Harvard University Health Services (HUHS) that acts as liaisons between Counseling and Mental Health Services (CAMHS) and the Harvard College community. We work collaboratively with CAMHS, the Harvard administration, and student communities to promote awareness of issues and improve accessibility to resources related to mental health and wellness. In an effort to do so, we strive to reduce stigma surrounding mental health and engage in outreach to address the specific needs of various communities on campus. We strive to encourage open conversation about matters of mental health and educate students about resources on campus. Ultimately, we hope to help the community to better understand issues of emotional well-being, recognize signs of students in distress, and feel comfortable navigating resources for support.

name: Aerospace & Defense Club
description: The mission of the Aerospace & Defense Club is to connect students with high-impact firms operating in those sectors, foster connections among students throughout the Cambridge area, and raise awareness of the increasing worldwide importance of aerospace and defense. Annual Events Technology and National Security Conference Aerospace & Defense Speaker Series Student Networking Event Series Recruiting Event Series
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Aerospace Medicine Association (AsMA) - HMS/MIT Student Chapter, "Doctors Without Gravity" (AsMA)
description: Doctors Without Gravity is the Harvard/MIT student chapter of the the Aerospace Medical Association (AsMA) with the Aerospace Medical Student and Resident Organization (AMSRO). We are a joint chapter between Harvard and MIT, the first of its kind! Our goal is to foster educational awareness and create opportunities in aerospace medicine, spaceflight biology, and human space exploration broadly. We hope to create a diverse collaborative community inclusive of everybody--from undergraduate and graduate students, to medical students, to faculty, and to all levels of training in between.

name: Africa Business Club
description: Twenty-seven years ago, African students at HBS saw the need to create an organization to elevate the African brand and highlight what it means be African, do business in Africa, and push for Africa’s development and prosperity. This mission remains unchanged. Today, ABC is one of the most successful student clubs at Harvard Business School, promoting inclusion of all African regions, and innovative thinking to inspire students to make a positive impact on the continent, while also serving as a two-sided gateway connecting the HBS community to the African continent and vice versa. Annual Events Africa Business Conference Regional Nights Club Website https://www.africa-hbsclub.com
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: African American Student Union
description: New members are first welcomed to the AASU family at our annual fall retreat. From there, they are supported throughout the RC year with informative workshops, panels and alumni events. These events primarily focus on academic excellence, recruiting / career support and community building. Many of our events are designed to engage the broader HBS and Harvard community and highlight the role of AASU member within their respective sessions, including community-wide discussion on The 1619 Project and the student-led “MyTakes,” and diversity-focused panels. The Naylor H. Fitzhugh Conference is the culminating event for AASU. It gives prospective and admitted students an opportunity to engage with the current AASU membership, facilitates networking between current students and alumni and provides a platform for the club to honor industry leaders — many of whom are AASU alumni. Annual Events H. Naylor Fitzhugh Conference Black Tech Masters Series Black New Venture Competition Fall/Spring Retreat Black History Month Celebration
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: African Law Association
description: The mission of Harvard Law School African Law Association ( HALA) is to unite African students and students interested in Africa, and increase awareness of legal, social and economic issues that shape and concern the continent of Africa.

name: AI Club
description: The mission of the AI Club is to bring technologists together at HBS. We want to keep our technical skills sharp and create accountability to learn and build while getting our MBAs.
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: AI Safety Team (AIST)
description: A community of Harvard students doing technical and policy research on reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI. Runs nine-week intro fellowships (Technical, Policy, and AI × Biorisk tracks) every semester and summer, meeting weekly in Harvard Square.
eligibility: Mostly Harvard undergraduate and graduate students and postdocs; some other Boston-area students
join_instructions: Apply to an intro fellowship; membership applications go to fellows after each fellowship. When applications are closed, the interest form on the Join page emails you when the next round opens.

name: Alliance for Israel
description: The Harvard Law School Alliance for Israel ( AFI) is a diverse student-run organization dedicated to fostering positive, truthful, and responsible discussion of issues affecting the Jewish State.

name: Alliance for Reproductive Justice
description: The Harvard Law School Alliance for Reproductive Justice (ARJ) seeks to promote the advancement of reproductive rights and reproductive justice through advocacy on our campus and in our communities, through public-education programming, including campus-wide teach-ins, and through monthly events on a wide range of topics related to reproductive justice: abortion access, reproductive and sexual healthcare, maternal health, racial justice, economic justice, and LGBTQ+ rights. ARJ approaches all our events and advocacy with an intersectional framework and subscribes to the following definition of reproductive justice (developed by Sister Song: Women of Color Reproductive Justice Collective): reproductive justice is the human right to maintain personal bodily autonomy, have children, not have children, and parent the children we have in safe and sustainable communities.

name: Alumni Relations & Global Outreach
description: Engage with the diverse community of 34,000 alumni through the Harvard Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School Alumni Association (GSAA), a network of scholars and professionals working around the globe. Our office sponsors a variety of opportunities for our alumni to stay connected with one another, with current students, and with Harvard.

name: American Constitution Society for Law & Policy of Harvard Law School
description: The Harvard Law School American Constitution Society for Law and Policy ( ACS) is comprised of law students, lawyers, scholars, judges, policymakers, activists and other concerned individuals who are working to ensure that the fundamental principles of human dignity, individual rights and liberties, genuine equality, and access to justice are in their rightful, central place in American law.

name: American Medical Association / Massachusetts Medical Society - HMS Students Chapter (AMA)
American Student Dental Association at Harvard School of Dental Medicine
description: Our mission at HSDM ASDA is to inspire and develop future leaders by fostering engagement with local, state, and national leaders in the dental community. We actively involve our members, alumni, faculty, and staff through educational lunch and learns, pre-dental outreach events, community service initiatives, and networking opportunities throughout Boston and beyond.

name: Animal Law Society
description: The Harvard Law School Animal Law Society is a group of students who care about animals and the issues facing them. HLS Animal Law Society was founded in 1995 as a student chapter of the Animal Legal Defense Fund , a national organization of lawyers engaged in litigation and legislative efforts on behalf of animals. HLS Animal Law Society has four major goals:

name: Animal Welfare Student Group at Harvard Griffin GSAS
description: The Animal Welfare Student Group at at Harvard GSAS is dedicated to the goal of providing education, awareness, and community spaces on animal welfare primarily for students at GSAS. The group also welcomes students in the Harvard community. Collectively, we aim to prevent animal cruelty, protect the environment, and safeguard public health. The activities of the AWSG at HGG shall include: promoting information on lifestyle changes, social gatherings, documentary screenings, and speaker events to protect animal welfare and share vegan options.

name: Antitrust Association
description: The Harvard Law School Antitrust Association ( HLSAA) aims to aid the law school community in understanding antitrust law. Our goal is to support and foster a community committed to the protection of consumers and the promotion of competitive markets.

name: ApiChorus: Harvard Hillel Jewish Student A Capella Group
Appalachian Harvard Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Appalachian Harvard Law Students Association (APPSA) is a community that brings together students with a background or interest in Appalachia. We support each other and the region, host cultural events, and share our identity with the rest of campus to shed light on one of America’s most misunderstood areas. All students with an interest are welcome, regardless of geographic origins!

name: Armed Forces Alumni Association
description: The mission of the Armed Forces Alumni Association (AFAA) is to assist in the professional development and job search process of members; to promote camaraderie among members; and to raise awareness and support for the military on the Harvard Business School campus. Annual Events AFAA Career Fair Veteran's Day Ball Military Visit Day Campaign for the New England Shelter for Homeless Veterans Panels and Mentorship Opportunities for Interview, Resume and Career Preparation Club Website http://www.afaahbsclub.com
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Armed Forces Association
description: The Harvard Law School Armed Forces Association (AFA) is an organization composed of veterans, active duty military service members, and those who are either interested in joining or supporting the Armed Forces of the United States of America.

name: Armenian Student Association at Harvard College
description: Promoting the appreciation and understanding of Armenian history, heritage and culture at Harvard College.

name: Armenian Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Armenian Students’ Association (ALSA) provides a forum for students to explore legal issues relevant to Armenia and Armenians. The Association nurtures deep and sustained engagement on topics including Armenian Genocide recognition and reparations; legal advocacy for endangered Christian minorities in Turkey, Syria, and the wider Middle East; and development and rule of law in the Republic of Armenia. In addition to cultivating legal discussion, ALSA also connects students to a wide array of Armenian-related educational, cultural, religious, and social programs.

name: Art Law Organization
description: The Harvard Law School Art Law Organization (HALO) is focused on the practice and study of art law and dedicated to giving students an opportunity to learn more about this area of the law and legal practice within it, as well as to building community for students around their shared interest. It achieves these goals by hosting events with lawyers working in the art world in various capacities, such as working for museums/galleries, foundations funding the arts, government arts organizations, and representing artists pro bono, as well as spanning various art law issues, including art-related contract drafting, copyright, provenance litigation, ownership litigation, repatriation litigation, and First Amendment issues. The organization also plans other art-law-related events, such as museum and gallery trips, as well as providing networking opportunities relating to art law practice.

name: Art Society
description: To promote the appreciation and creation of art of all forms within the HBS community. Annual Events Student Photography and Art Show Trips: New York City Art Trek, Art Basel Miami Beach Trek Museum Tours Private Collection Visits Sundance Film Festival
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Artificial Intelligence Association
description: The mission of the Harvard Law School AI Student Association (AIA) is to convene law students interested in the governance of advanced AI systems and to ensure that transformational AI technologies have positive consequences for the world. AIA hosts regular student meet-ups, convenes speaking events and panels, and promotes public interest careers related to AI. To contact us, please reach out at ai@mail.law.harvard.edu.

name: Arts - Student Center Fellows
description: Welcome to your creative home at Harvard Griffin GSAS. Student Center Arts is all about building community through shared expression. We invite you to unwind and untangle your mind with our cozy knitting circles, connect with peers on the dance floor through our spirited Salsa and Bachata lessons, and discover the beauty of our city together through group trips to world-class museums and theaters. Come for the art, stay for the friendship.

name: Asia Law Society
description: The Harvard Law School’s Asia Law Society ( HALS) is a prominent organization at Harvard Law School that brings together students with a common interest in Asia. HALS is extremely diverse and international, with past and current members from not only East Asia and North America, but also from South Asia, Latin America, and beyond.

name: Asian Baptist Student Koinonia at Harvard Griffin GSAS
description: Asian Baptist Student Koinonia at Harvard Griffin GSAS is concerned with the religious, social, and cultural issues regarding Christianity and Asians and Christianity. The group will seek to promote greater awareness and understanding of these issues in the Harvard community, and specifically among Harvard Griffin GSAS students, by appropriate means such as Bible studies, publications, meetings, seminars, and other educational activities.  The group’s activities and services will be available to all members of the Harvard University community, regardless of race, creed, color, sex, sexual orientation, age, or physical disability. We're a group of Christian graduate students who are excited to know God more, to study the truths of the Bible together, and to share God’s love with the Harvard grad student community. Our activities include weekly Bible studies, sports, games, meals, and mission trips. Whatever your background, we hope you'll join us to explore life from God's perspective and build meaningful, fun friendships!

name: Asian Pacific American Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Asian Pacific American Law Students Association (APALSA) is a political, academic, community service, and social group dedicated to fostering a supportive atmosphere for Asian Pacific American students at Harvard Law School. APALSA strives to promote a greater understanding of Asian Pacific American issues and culture, serve as a vehicle for Asian Pacific American political activity, and provide a social and academic network for Asian Pacific Americans and the Harvard Law School community.

name: Asian Student Arts Project
description: The purpose of ASAP is to provide the network and resources for Pan-Asian and Pan-Asian-American students across multiple disciplines including theater, film, dance, music, comedy, writing, entertainment, media, and more to make art and create a community for these artists. ASAP aims to celebrate the community, experience, culture, and history of Asian students at Harvard with events such as group discussions, movie screenings, workshops, open-mic nights, group outings, panels, and large- and small-scale performances and theatrical productions.

name: Asian-Affinity Business Association
description: The Asian-American Business Association (AABA) provides a community for the promotion, understanding, and cross-cultural exchange of Asian and Asian-American business, social, academic, cultural, and political initiatives. Annual Events Cabin Fall Retreat Las Vegas Spring Retreat Spring Soirée Formal Small Group Dinners Faculty Dinners Mid-Autumn Festival Celebration Lunar New Year Celebration Movie Showings Dim Sum Brunches Thanksgiving Potluck Portrait Project Exam Study Sessions & Snack Breaks Volunteer Outings Inter-MBA and Cross-Harvard Mixers And More!
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Association for Insight & Meditation
description: The Harvard Law School Association for Insight & Meditation ( AIM) seeks to build and grow a community of future lawyers who aspire to understand the nature of consciousness through Buddhist and other meditation traditions. It serves as a home for those already engaged in the investigation of lived experience and as an introduction to meditation & insight for those who are unfamiliar. AIM encourages members to aim attention back upon itself to better understand the way it shapes experience. It is grounded in the principles of non-dogmatic, experiential learning. Instead of saying “this is true” it says “I find this to be true about my experience. See if it is true for you, right here and now.”

name: Association for Law and Business
description: The Harvard Law School Association for Law and Business (HALB) connects students with prominent leaders across the business and legal communities. Each year, HALB hosts numerous speakers to discuss their careers and areas of expertise, while also creating outside opportunities for members to meet like-minded students and practitioners interested in non-legal business careers. Over the past several years we have hosted events with luminaries across business, law, and finance, as well as those featuring most of the top law firms, investment banks, and management consultancies.

name: Association for Real Estate and Law
description: The Harvard Law School Association for Real Estate and Law (HREL) is an active community for Harvard Law School students to explore their interests in all facets of the real estate industry, including legal practice, development, investing, financing, and land-use policy. HREL brings distinguished practitioners to campus as guest speakers, organizes career treks, hosts networking and professional training sessions, and advocates for additional real estate focused academic offerings on campus. HREL welcomes all current students and alumni looking to further develop their industry knowledge, connect with peers who have similar interests, and pursue professional opportunities.

name: Association of PhD students in Architecture, Landscape Architecture, and Urban Planning
description: Organized wholly by GSAS PhD students, PhD Talks is an annual speaker series dedicated to the exploration of interdisciplinary themes that engage issues of space. PhD Talks is an opportunity for our program, which is deeply interdisciplinary, and includes participation from the departments of History, American Studies, Art History, Sociology, Philosophy, History of Science, Anthropology and Film and Visual Studies to come together as an intellectual unit and assert its relevance within the context of a professional school, the Graduate School of Design. It is also a chance for us to showcase the more historical and theoretical work being produced to the wider GSAS and Harvard community. The PhD students also sponsor conferences such as the New England chapter of the Society of Architectural Historians Graduate Student Symposium, which takes place every year at a university in the Boston area, and at Harvard approximately every three years. These conferences offer the opportunity for graduate students in the department to connect with PhD students and faculty at other local institutions, as well as to share their research in a conference setting.

name: AstroGrad Network
description: The goal of the AstroGrad Network (AGN) is to facilitate social events and professional development programs for graduate students at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics.

name: At the Crossroads
description: At the Crossroads is a student-led space for building connections across the different fields and subfields of Harvard’s Department of Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations (NELC), while also welcoming students from adjacent departments and programs whose work intersects with ours.

name: Athletics and Outings - Student Center Fellows
description: The Athletics and Outings Fellows organize events to explore the city of Boston and surrounding New England and stay active. We love to go on outdoor adventures, like biking, skiing, and foraging, and we also provide affordable tickets to professional sports events and theater shows in downtown Boston. Looking to stay active, meet new people, and have fun along the way? Whether you’re a seasoned athlete or just want to try something new, Student Center Athletics & Outings has something for you! Is there an event you really want to go to, or a local trip you really want to take with other students or an intramural sports team you want to join? We want to hear from you!

name: Australian & New Zealand Club
description: To promote the Australian and New Zealand (ANZ) region at Harvard Business School by facilitating activities for members, raising the profiles of Australia and New Zealand as places to do business, and fostering networking opportunities between MBA students and Australasian businesses. Annual Events Down Under Ball
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

description: To celebrate Australian culture.

name: B-School Blades
description: Our goal is to provide a forum where hockey players of all skill levels are able to compete, improve and enjoy hockey by organizing weekly practices and games and attending tournaments. The club also intends to develop a strong sense of camaraderie by organizing monthly social events around the sport we love. Annual Events HBS Tournament Dartmouth Tournament Outings to Bruins games
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: BBS Peer Mentors
description: The BBS Peer Mentors are a group of upper year BBS students dedicated to promoting community amongst BBS students and to providing advice and support to our fellow BBSers. We are a diverse group who are available for one-on-one meetings to discuss any challenges students may be facing. We also work with groups of first year students to answer questions and welcome them to the BBS community. Additionally, we hold quarterly community building events for all BBS students. Learn more about our 2022-23 BBS Peer Mentors in the flyer below! (Harvard sign-in required)

name: Beeritas
description: The Harvard Law School Beeritas, a student-run organization, is the official Beer Appreciation Society of Harvard Law School. That’s right, if you were afraid your beer-drinking days were over now that you are a big bad law student, we’re here for you. Come join us for bi-weekly tastings, beer-themed events, and trips to local breweries throughout the semester to take advantage of HLS’s location in such a great city for beer. All in all, Beeritas is a place for people who care about beer in all shapes, sizes, and styles. If all of this sounds too good to be true, then welcome to Beeritas!

name: Bell Collective for Critical Race Theory
description: The Harvard Law School Bell Collective for Critical Race Theory is to build learning spaces at HLS dedicated to Critical Race Theory as a lens with which to view and critique the law, where students can study and understand law, policy, and customs as an unjust system of domination perpetuated by historically privileged groups, and that build a community that seeks to reimagine lawyering as a profession.

name: Bengali Association of Students at Harvard College
description: The Bengali Association of Students at Harvard (BASHA) is a cultural organization concerned with promoting the unique aspects of Bengali culture and fostering community among students with roots in Bangladesh, West Bengal, and the diaspora, as well as others with interest in the region’s rich history and traditions. Through our various social, cultural, and academic programming, we seek to provide members of the Harvard community with a home away from home, as that is what basha (বাসা) means.

name: Beyond Dance Club
description: Beyond Dance is an organization which seeks to connect members of the HBS community who share a passion for dance, to provide an avenue for practicing and performing, and to expose members of the community to new styles of dance from across the globe.
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Biomedical Graduate Student Organization
description: Our goal at the Biomedical Graduate Student Organization (BGSO) is to enrich and foster a sense of community among PhD students in the Life Sciences at Harvard Medical School through a series of social and academic initiatives. BGSO represents the over 700 PhD students enrolled in HMS-based graduate programs affiliated with the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GSAS). These include the Biological and Biomedical Sciences (BBS), Virology, Immunology, Neuroscience, Speech and Hearing Bioscience and Technology (SHBT), and Biomedical Informatics (BMI). BGSO is also a student funding entity which allocates resources to Longwood-based student groups for social and/or academic activities.

name: Biostatistics Peer Mentor Program
description: The Biostatistics PhD Peer Mentor Program aims to create a network of guidance, community, and support for Biostatistics students as they move through their PhD years. The Peer Mentor Program matches mentors to mentees, organizes activities to bolster mentorship, and hosts student support seminars that provide advice and enhance the well-being and success of early-year doctoral students.

name: Biostatistics PhD Student Committee
description: The Biostatistics PhD Student Committee is the official student body organization that organizes programming including social and outreach events for the graduate community, and advocates for graduate students in the department. The PhD student committee is dedicated to promoting community among students, facilitating communication with administration, and fostering collaboration with the wider Harvard community.

name: Bitcoin & Crypto Club
description: The Bitcoin & Crypto Club’s mission is to: i) provide an educational foundation for people interested in learning about bitcoin and crypto technologies, and ii) increase exposure and access to various industry experts, allowing students to learn about emerging applications, cultivate relationships, and facilitate employment opportunities in the space. Annual Events 101 Educational Series Annual Trek Bitcoin & Crypto Conference
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Black Investment Club
description: The Black Investment Club (BIC) seeks to address the massive underrepresentation of black investors in venture capital, private equity, and investment management by creating a platform to empower and advance the interests of our community. We leverage our relationships with sponsoring organizations, alumni, and the HBS community to facilitate relationship building and technical development specifically tailored for the needs of black investors. By cultivating and growing a strong pipeline of qualified students specifically interested in buy-side investing, our mission is to make it easier for firms to hire diverse candidates.
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Black Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Black Law Students Association (HBLSA) was founded in 1967. Today, HBLSA has grown to become the largest chapter in the National Black Law Students Association. Counting over 160 members annually, HBLSA reflects the strong Black community that is so integral to the diversity of Harvard Law School. The Black Law Students Association of Harvard Law School exists for the support, guidance and direction of Black students in academic, professional and social endeavors.

name: Blockchain and FinTech Initiative
description: The Harvard Law School Blockchain and FinTech Initiative ( HLSBFI) is the first student-led initiative aimed at promoting education and career-development for law students interested in working in industries that utilize blockchain and financial technologies. The Initiative will expose students to the plethora of legal issues that arise in enterprise and institutional applications of blockchain and financial technology. We hope to facilitate learning within the Harvard Law School community and beyond by hosting speakers, offering hands-on projects, and connecting students to scholars, practitioners and industry specialists. We hope to encourage students to build relationships, and serve as a hub to deliver internships and full-time employment to students passionate about the impact of technology on the financial industry. Finally, we hope to establish Harvard Law School as a leader scholarship on the legal issues affecting blockchain application and the financial technology industry.

name: Board of Student Advisers
description: The Harvard Law School Board of Student Advisers (BSA) is a student organization charged with providing several essential services to the Harvard Law School community: we serve as teaching assistants in the First Year Legal Research and Writing Program, as peer advisers to members of the first-year class and transfer students, and as administrators of the Ames Moot Court competition. Our Mission is to build a community, both among first-year students and among the diverse student body of the Harvard Law School. We are unique among student organizations in that our role is both to provide opportunities for students to engage with intellectually challenging legal problems and to serve as a support network for students going through the challenging academic and personal transition to law school.

name: Boat Club
description: The Boat Club at HBS strives to provide an opportunity for HBS students to row and will work to promote the sport of rowing within the HBS community. Annual Events Head of the Charles Regatta The Graduate Schools Championship Regatta
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: BPH Peer Mentor Team
description: The BPH Peer Mentor Team is comprised of BPH students from across G-years, working towards the common goal of supporting peers and each other throughout their graduate studies. Students are matched with peer mentors based on defined needs and interests to develop strong connections and effective mentor-mentee partnerships. The trained and diverse team of peer mentors connects with mentees through both one-on-one meetings and group activities to foster community engagement and provide peer support.

name: Brazilian Studies Association
description: The Harvard Law School Brazilian Studies Association (HLS BR) is an institution that intends to promote the collaboration between students, scholars, professionals, and individuals who are interested in discussing various issues related to Brazil and Brazilian culture.

description: The mission of the Brew Club is to cultivate a community of beer enthusiasts to connect them to the growing beer industry and each other through brewery tours, beer education, and social events. description: The mission of the Canadian Club is to provide a sense of community for Canadians studying at HBS and to promote an awareness of Canada within the HBS community. We also seek to foster ties between current HBS students and HBS Canadian alumni. description: In addition to providing practical support, eh? The Harvard Law School Canadian Law Students Association (CLSA) will also provide a place for community. Providing peer-to-peer support within the Canadian legal market, links to alumni, and advice on which courses travel well from HLS.

description: The Harvard Law School Caribbean Law Students Association (CLSA) seeks to highlight legal issues impacting the Caribbean, celebrate the achievements of Caribbean people, and create an affinity space for those who identify with Caribbean cultures.

name: Catholic Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Catholic Law Students Association ( CLSA) is the on-campus home for Catholic students, faculty, and friends in the Harvard Law School community. The Catholic community at HLS is open to anyone and everyone who is curious about spiritual enrichment, community service, and fellowship.

name: Catholic Student Association
description: The Catholic Student Association fosters a welcoming Catholic community at HBS. We support students and their partners with faith, formation, and fellowship opportunities. We welcome people at every stage of their faith journey and promote thoughtful conversation about the Catholic faith and its application to our personal and professional lives. Annual Events Mass and community dinners Bible Study Eucharistic Adoration Men's and Women's Group Retreat and faith-based excursions Catholic speakers
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

Central & Eastern European Club
description: The primary mission of the Emerging Europe Association is to facilitate professional, cultural and social activities aimed at HBS students interested in Emerging Europe. To join our mailing list, please email the president at ttalks@hms.harvard.edu. Chalk Talks, a Harvard Griffin GSAS Student Group, meets monthly to share cool science, philosophical, and historical topics in chalk talk format. A chalk talk is a talk given using chalk and a chalkboard as a means to communicate ideas (no slides!). Topics have included life origins, theoretical experiment proposals, bioethics, the history of splitting an atom, and the world’s largest known bacteria. The format is roughly 7-10 min chalk talk with 5 min questions. Participants are required to give a talk to attend. Once or twice a year, faculty are invited to participate, promoting faculty-student discussion and collaboration.

name: Conflux
description: As technology continues to advance and play an increasingly central role in our lives, the intersection of art and technology helps us understand the complex and rapidly changing relationship between humanity and technology. Conflux provides a supportive ecosystem for artists to challenge and critique the dominant narratives and power structures that shape our society, and for technologists to consider the ethical and social implications of their work. In recent years, our vibrant intellectual community has brought together around 60 S.J.D. candidates—most of whom are in residence and hail from 25 to 30 countries worldwide. description: Watch our welcome video here! name: Graduate Residence Halls Council at Harvard Griffin GSAS
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Residence Halls are a great place to live while studying at Harvard. The purpose of the Graduate Residence Halls Council (GRHC) at Harvard Griffin GSAS, formerly known as the Graduate Dormitory Council (GDC), is to foster community among the residents of the Harvard Griffin GSAS halls via various social activities through the year. The GRHC maintains close communication with residents on important Residence Halls issues, in coordination with the Harvard Griffin GSAS Office of Residential Life and the Office of Student Services. The GRHC also promotes and organizes social activities in the Residence Halls, and the GRHC provides funding for dorm-wide social events sponsored by Resident Advisors or residents.

name: Graduate Society of Underrepresented Students in STEM, a Harvard Griffin GSAS Student Group
description: STEM, a Harvard Griffin GSAS Student Group About The Graduate Society of Underrepresented Students in STEM, a Harvard Griffin GSAS Student Group (GSUSS) is dedicated to providing a space for Harvard Griffin GSAS students to come together throughout their time at Harvard for academic and personal community and support. We want to provide a space for like-minded students to share their lives inside and outside of Harvard. A 2015 report from the Council of Graduate Schools showed that in regard to underrepresented student graduate degree completion “racial/ethnic differences persist after controlling for the main and interactive effects of gender and field in seven-year completion and attrition”. Our group supports the well-being and long-term retention of members through social and networking events. It will be a welcoming space where members can talk freely about topics like the “unspoken curriculum” of being a Harvard Griffin GSAS student with regards to work/life balance, doing research, lab culture, advisor relationships, giving scientific talks, etc. Through weekly meetings and a yearly wellness retreat, GSUSS will be a place where underrepresented Harvard Griffin GSAS STEM students can celebrate with and support each other through the many triumphs and setbacks that may arise throughout any graduate career. We will also invite faculty speakers with expertise in diversity issues to engage the Harvard Griffin GSAS community on issues of diversity and equity in STEM.

name: Greater China Club
description: The Greater China Club is aspired: (1) To engage HBS students in one of the world's most dynamic economies on business, economic, and social issues; (2) To create a platform for HBS community to share business knowledge, entrepreneurial ideas, industry experiences, and leadership practices related to the Greater China region; (3)To spread best management practices, channel global talents, and promote economic and social transformation in the world's most populous region. Annual Events China Small Enterprise Forum Speaker Series Trek
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Greener Scott Scholars Mentorship Program
description: 1. Greener Scott Scholars will promote mentoring between graduate and undergraduate students on an individual and group basis increasing students’ self-confidence and their sense of belonging. 2. Greener Scott Scholars will improve mentee/mentor interpersonal, leadership, and relationship skills while supporting the mentee as they adjust to Harvard’s culture and environment. 3. Greener Scott Scholars will provide opportunities for specialized engagement and growth, as well as access to Harvard faculty, staff, and experts who understand minority dynamics through lectures, panels, and/or workshops for the collective group via club-wide 3-4 meetings per semester.

name: Group for Undergraduate Students in Statistics at Harvard College
Harvard Art Museums
description: Free every day (open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am–5pm) and just steps away from Harvard Square, the Harvard Art Museums welcome visitors from around the corner and the world to enjoy one of the largest and most renowned art collections in North America. Masterpieces from our collection of more than a quarter million works include paintings by Vincent van Gogh, Claude Monet, John Singer Sargent, and Jackson Pollock; contemporary works by living artists such as, Rashid Johnson, Carlos Amorales, Arlene Shechet, and Kerry James Marshall; and a variety of remarkable objects from ancient cultures in the Mediterranean, Near East, and Far East. In addition, an exciting lineup of special exhibitions gives us the chance to showcase an even wider range of works spanning diverse media, genres, and eras. The Calderwood Courtyard is any visitor’s first stop; it offers not only panoramic views into surrounding galleries and up through the museums’ five main floors, but also a gathering space to meet friends, a comfortable spot to enjoy a cup of coffee in Jenny’s Cafe, and access to the array of gifts, books, and memorabilia available in our museum shop. Pop in for a quick look or stay a while—either way, you are welcome here!

name: Harvard Black Men's Forum
description: The Harvard Black Men's Forum catalyzes the agency of Harvard undergraduate black men. We support our members through our core pillars of brotherhood, masculinity, and fidelity. Working with faculty and national figures, we provide a forum for discussion and action on issues pertinent to our body. We additionally seek to provide support for disadvantaged members of this country through various service initiatives like the David Walkers Scholars Program, a tutoring and mentoring program.

name: Harvard Buddhist Studies Forum
description: The Harvard Buddhist Studies Forum (HBSF) is a long-standing lecture series at Harvard University at which scholars are invited to present on a topic related to the field of Buddhist Studies. The HBSF strives to promote a wide range of disciplines, geographical areas, and methodologies. Contact Joie Chen (chens@g.harvard.edu) to be added to the email list.

name: Harvard Canadian Club
description: The Harvard College Canadian Club is concerned with fostering community among Canadian students and Canadian enthusiasts at Harvard, celebrating Canadian culture and heritage, and serving as a resource for students interested in Canada and Canadian affairs.

name: Harvard Caribbean Club
description: The mission of HCC is to foster a sense of community among Caribbean students and students interested in the Caribbean at Harvard by celebrating Caribbean culture and heritage. Furthermore, HCC shall aim to promote a greater awareness regarding the people, affairs, and culture of the Caribbean throughout the Harvard Community.

name: Harvard Chemistry Club
description: The Harvard Chemistry Club serves as a meeting place for undergraduate chemists at Harvard and a venue for chemical education initiatives tailored for undergraduates. Open to concentrators in Chemistry, Chemistry and Physics, and Chemical and Physical Biology, as well as to all students interested in chemistry, the Harvard Chemistry Club holds regular social gatherings, faculty dinners, seminars, and advising events.

name: Harvard College Albanian Students Association
description: The Albanian Students Association is an organization that unites students of Albanian origin and students interested in Albanian culture, history, and contemporary issues. The organization will raise awareness of social, economic, and political conditions that affect Albanians throughout the world through: community discussions, cultural (music/food/film) events, forums, and networking events.

Harvard College Bowl

description: Founded in 2004 by a group of Nigerian undergraduate students, the Harvard College Nigerian Students Association has grown both in numbers and respect, becoming one of the premier organizations for students on campus. Based on the shared culture and values of Nigerian and Nigerian American students, Harvard NSA has not only created a community for Nigerians to come together but has also spread an appreciation for the Nigerian culture throughout campus through various activities and events.

Harvard College Queer Students Association
description: The Harvard College Queer Students Association (QSA) is a resource organization concerned with improving the visibility, strength, and support of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, questioning, and allied students, initiatives, organizations, and communities, in recognition of the marginalization that exists as the result of stigmatized identities. This group seeks to promote community and awareness of and be a resource with respect to the social, socioeconomic, political, educational, and cultural issues surrounding queer identities and sexualities in the form of events driven toward creating safe spaces in collaboration with other groups, institutions, and communities.

name: Harvard College Russian-Speaking Students Association
description: Provide exposure to Russian-speaking cultures, societies, and the language to help the student population become more informed on Russian-speaking countries. Allow heritage/native speakers to find a community of people with a similar background where they are welcomed and encouraged to explore their identity. Immerse students of the Russian language in the cultures and promote language learning. Provide students with an open floor to speak freely about their experiences and ideas through events and meetings. Create a sense of community amongst all Russian-speakers.

Harvard College Student Chapter of the Massachusetts Menstrual Equity Coalition
Harvard College Students American Lung Cancer Screening Initiative
description: The Harvard chapter of the American Lung Cancer Screening Initiative (ALCSI) is dedicated to promoting awareness, education, and early detection of lung cancer. Our mission is to empower our community with knowledge about the importance of lung cancer screening, advocate for accessible screening programs, and support research initiatives aimed at reducing lung cancer mortality. Through collaboration, outreach, and education, we strive to make a meaningful impact in the fight against lung cancer.

name: Harvard College Students for Uyghur Solidarity
Harvard College Students Piano Society
description: Established in 2000, the Harvard College Students Piano Society (HCPS) is dedicated to fostering piano performance, pedagogy, and appreciation both within and beyond the Harvard community. We are devoted to forging a more intimate and united community of musicians, providing performance opportunities for student pianists and connecting pianists with the wider Harvard arts community. HCPS hosts masterclasses, workshops, and recital series with pianists from around the world. We welcome both amateur and professional pianists, and even non-musicians who just love music.

name: Harvard College Turkish Student Association
description: HCTSA's mission is to: (1) promote an inclusive community for Turkish students at Harvard. (2) promote the exchange of ideas for a better understanding of Turkish people, their culture and history. (3) To present the interests of its members in dealing with the Harvard University Administration and various student organizations, (4) To provide an environment for interaction among its members, their families, international communities, Harvard University students, staff, and similar college associations.

name: Harvard College Union Society
description: The Harvard College Union Society is an undergraduate community dedicated to free inquiry and civil discourse. Our group debates the most salient issues facing Harvard and the larger American body politic without fear in the face of controversy.

name: Harvard Community of Humanists, Atheists, and Agnostics
Harvard Composers Association
description: The mission of HCA is to provide undergraduate students with pre-professional experience in composing, producing, and administration that they otherwise would not find through classes in the Harvard Music Department or elsewhere in the University. Harvard music classes, while they may offer performance opportunities for new works, do not offer room for students to understand the production of their works or to interact and organize musicians in a way that will be required of them professionally. With the decline of record company budgets, nowadays all musicians are essentially independent business owners, and sufficient resources are needed to replicate that type of environment. Additionally, all HCA composers will have primary ownership of their recordings, allowing them to publish works online to build portfolios. This decision is in line with the current trend seen at Berklee and other institutions to allow student ownership of works created while on campus. Students will also explore the legal side of the music business to understand contract terminology and publishing.

name: Harvard Debate Council
description: Founded in 1892, the Debate Council is one of the oldest and proudest intercollegiate policy debate programs in the nation. Committed to excellence in both competitive and educational achievement, Harvard Debate has won the National Debate Tournament (NDT) seven times, most recently in 2016, and finished second five times, since the tournament was first held in 1947. The NDT records show that Harvard Debate has been invited to attend the tournament every year since 1954 – a record of consistency unmatched by any other school. In recent years, Harvard Debaters have won every major national policy debate invitational. For two years in a row, in 2016 and 2017, Harvard won the Rex Copeland Award for the Top First Round At-Large Team at the NDT awarded to the team with the best individual record in the regular season.

name: Harvard Government Graduate Student Organization
description: The Gov GSA works to promote transparency and inclusion of student voices in the department, liaises with faculty and administrators, fosters professional and personal community within the department, and promotes student well-being. It consists of four standing committees (Wellness, Social, Diversity, and International Students), in addition to several ad-hoc committees. name: Harvard Graduate School of Education
description: HGSE PhD G1s is the first-year student community for the Ph.D. in Education, a doctoral program offered jointly by Harvard Griffin GSAS and the Harvard Graduate School of Education. Our members span the program’s three concentrations: Culture, Institutions, and Society; Education Policy and Program Evaluation; and Human Development, Learning and Teaching. They bring training from fields as varied as economics, psychology, sociology, history, anthropology, and cognitive science. We aim to build connections across concentrations and disciplines by organizing study sessions, community-building activities, and informal gatherings. These give members a place to share their work, learn from one another, and support each other through the first year of doctoral study, a critical phase in the academic journey.

name: Harvard Graduate Students in Linguistics
description: The goals of Harvard Graduate Students in Linguistics (HGSL) are twofold: primarily, we strive to create an environment conducive to community building, by organizing social events (for example, the departmental Happy Hours and Study Breaks during the exam period), and implementing various community-building projects within our community (for example, the yearly Photo Contest). Secondly, we aim to provide opportunities for graduate students to acquire practical skills pertinent to our field of study, specifically those not otherwise offered by the department or GSAS. We do so by organizing workshops on specific topics, based on suggestions from the student body, led by members of the HGSL executive committee and fellow graduate student volunteers. For example, we organized a two-session workshop titled: 'Praat for Linggrads', which taught students how to use software that is useful for various linguistic studies, and we sometimes offer a similar workshop on LaTeX.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS
description: The Harvard Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences is where scholarship and innovation meet, where ideas are challenged and theories developed, where new knowledge is created, and where scholars emerge. We actively recruit and cultivate a diverse community of students across 58 fields of study. Throughout the year, Harvard Griffin GSAS hosts a variety of events for both incoming and current students.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Badminton Club
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Badminton Club aims to create and sustain an inclusive, welcoming, and fun environment that learns and enjoys the game of badminton together in the Harvard Griffin GSAS community. The group promotes a healthy lifestyle in the spirit of fair play and provides the opportunity for students to unwind from the stresses of graduate life. We welcome all levels and provide opportunities for training, group play, and tournament competitions to everyone./

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Biotechnology Club
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Biotechnology Club is a student organization that provides educational programs and hosts events that allow members to explore the world of business and biotechnology. The Biotechnology Club's mission is to bridge the gap between industry and academia by providing the education, the skill set, and the network for Harvard Griffin GSAS students to succeed in the life sciences industry.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Breakdance Club
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Breakdance Club is dedicated to the goal of providing members of the Harvard community, and specifically for all students at Harvard Griffin GSAS, space for the art and practice of hip hop street dances. The activities of HGGBC shall include, but not limited to: providing instruction in hip hop street dance styles such as breaking (“breakdancing”), conducting practice sessions for beginners and experienced dancers, participating in competitions, called jams, throughout the region to develop our competitive abilities, arranging watch-party socials for major competitions such as Red Bull, the Olympics, and other broadcasted jams, and hosting workshops with guest speakers about the culture of hip hop. We aim to cultivate a safe and welcoming space for all students at Harvard Griffin GSAS of all skill levels and backgrounds to learn more about breaking and street dance culture.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Business Club
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Business Club (hereafter referred to as HGBC) is dedicated to providing business education and business-related career development resources to the Harvard Griffin GSAS community. We also seek to provide networking opportunities for students in Harvard Griffin GSAS interested in business. Among the activities organized by the HGGBC are a 10-session business course offering an overview of the material typically covered in the first year of an MBA program, networking events for students in Harvard Griffin GSAS to interact with other students and business professionals, and a seminar series featuring professionals in business-or finance-related fields, such as entrepreneurs, venture capitalists, executives and investment bankers, and. The HGGBC will inform the Harvard Griffin GSAS community about sponsored events through, at minimum, its listserv and website.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Catholic Graduate Student Association
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Catholic Graduate Student Association provides an opportunity for Catholic graduate students in Harvard Griffin GSAS to meet one another socially and spiritually through monthly dinners, discussion groups, Mass and devotions, and volunteer service. Our goals include increasing a sense of community among Catholics on campus, heightening the visibility of Catholicism at Harvard University, especially within Harvard Griffin GSAS, investigating the place of Catholicism in an academic environment, promoting its connection to intellectual life, and encouraging exploration of the Catholic tradition./p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Chinese Students and Scholars Association
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Chinese Students and Scholars Association (HCSSA) is dedicated to supporting and enriching the experience of Chinese students and scholars as well as any one interested in Chinese culture at Harvard Griffin GSAS. Through a variety of social, intellectual, and cultural activities, we seek to promote Chinese culture, foster cross-cultural understanding, and build a vibrant and inclusive community that enriches campus life. HCSSA welcomes all students and scholars at Harvard Griffin GSAS to join our organization and participate in our activities. Please follow our WeChat Official Account (ID: HCSSA) for more events information.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Consulting Club

HGCC sponsors many programs to assist Harvard Griffin GSAS students on their consulting job/span span style="font-weight: 400;"hunt, with an emphasis on networking events, consulting panels, interview workshops, and case competitions./span/p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Dragon Boat Team

Founded in 1999 by members of the Dudley House crew team, the Harvard Griffin GSAS Dragon Boat Team is among the earliest dragon boat teams in Boston. As a member of the International Collegiate Dragon Boat Federation, the team competes throughout the Northeast region and internationally./p

The Harvard Griffin GSAS Dragon Boat Team promotes the sport and culture of dragon boating for individuals of the Harvard community and specifically for students affiliated with the Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GSAS), provides access to dragon boat practice sessions and races for its members, and promotes a culture of sportsmanship and mutual respect for one another./p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Entrepreneurs Association
description: Harvard Griffin GSAS Entrepreneurs Association (Harvard Griffin GEA) is dedicated to increasing the awareness of entrepreneurship and innovation among members of the Harvard community. Through speaker panels, roundtables, pitch events, workshops, and seminars, Harvard GEC provides opportunities for networking, sharing, and growth within and beyond the Harvard Community.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Episcopal Student Association
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Episcopal Student Association is a community that proclaims Christ’s life, death, and resurrection; embraces faith, mystery, and doubt; and strives to love like Jesus through the grace of the Holy Spirit. We pray, serve our neighbors, and challenge one another to grow in faith. In partnership with The Episcopal Chaplaincy at Harvard (ECH) and the Episcopal Students at Harvard College (ESHC), we seek to provide an intentional space for Harvard Griffin GSAS students to participate in the rich traditions of the Episcopal Church while fostering a strong sense of community and fellowship. Graduate school provides a unique opportunity for introspection and growth. We seek to provide a space for spiritual exploration for all students, regardless of whether they are new to the faith, grew up Episcopalian, or are simply curious to learn about our tradition. We hold Eucharist services followed by a communal dinner every Sunday evening during the academic year, host weekly Bible studies, and organize pilgrimages to sacred sites both locally in New England and internationally. All meetings are optional, and members are encouraged to participate as much or as little as they feel called to do./p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Film Club
description: The mission of the Harvard Griffin GSAS Film Club is to create community at Harvard Griffin GSAS through a shared love of film; monthly film screenings on campus, visual literacy discussions, and social events. We will bring together thinkers and makers from around Harvard Griffin GSAS and our wider community, these include visiting filmmakers, to share/present the movies that have had a profound impact on their lives and work.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Korea Society Club
description: Harvard Griffin GSAS Korea Society Club brings together Korean students and students who are interested in Korean culture throughout the Harvard Griffin GSAS community, while also aiming to advance the cultural and academic understanding of activities on campus and to encourage interaction with each other on campus. Activities include, but are not limited to: social and cultural events such as welcome events for incoming students, Early Spring Gala with MIT students, chamber concerts, academic events on Korea-related issues, and offering information related to Korean companies. This group is open to all students at Harvard Griffin GSAS./p
eligibility: Open to all students at Harvard Griffin GSAS

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Photo Society
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Photo Society is dedicated to providing photography resources and photography activities for members of the Harvard Griffin GSAS community. The activities include but are not limited to: providing freelancing opportunities around campus, organizing photo walks and gallery visits around Cambridge and Boston, connecting with local artists and photographers, hosting workshops on photo taking and developing/editing techniques, and hosting photo contests and events for showcasing personal projects. The club will also focus on building a social community of photographers for Harvard Griffin GSAS students./p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Poker Club
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Poker Club is a student organization dedicated to building a welcoming and intellectually engaging community around the game of poker. The Club promotes poker as a game of skill involving probability, statistics, psychology, strategic thinking, and decision-making. Through free-play games, workshops, and educational programming, the Club provides Harvard Griffin GSAS students with opportunities to learn, practice, and socialize in a collaborative environment. All Club activities are strictly free of cost and are conducted for recreational, educational, and social purposes only, without gambling, wagering, or entry fees. The Club also promotes responsible gaming culture and awareness./p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Polish Student Association
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Polish Student Association (HPSA) is dedicated to building a community among Harvard Griffin GSAS students with an interest in Polish culture, history, and heritage and welcomes participation from the broader Harvard community. The association organizes social and cultural events—such as food tastings (e.g., pierogi or pączki for Fat Thursday), movie screenings (by famous Polish filmmakers and about Polish history/culture) with discussion sessions, guest speaker & meet-greet events and more—to share and celebrate Polish culture. The group welcomes everyone regardless of their cultural background./p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Science Policy Group
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Science Policy Group is dedicated to providing members of the Harvard community, and in particular Harvard Griffin GSAS students, with opportunities to develop the knowledge and skills by which scientists can most effectively influence public policymaking. The group is open to all students at Harvard Griffin GSAS, regardless of whether they study science.
eligibility: Open to all students at Harvard Griffin GSAS, regardless of whether they study sci

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Singaporean and Malaysian Association
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Singaporean and Malaysian Association (SAMA) aims to help build ties within the Singaporean and Malaysian communities in Harvard Griffin GSAS, and to share Singaporean and Malaysian culture with the Harvard community and other interested individuals, by organizing and promoting a series of social, cultural and intellectual activities./p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Sinophone Debate Student Association
description:
The Harvard Griffin GSAS Sinophone Debate Student Association (HGG SDSA) is committed to cultivating a dynamic and inclusive community of debaters, open to students across Harvard Griffin GSAS and other community members. The term ‘Sinophone’ refers specifically to the use of Chinese languages, which includes all speakers of Mandarin and Cantonese regardless of their ethnicity, nationality, or culture. Sinophone debate serves as a vehicle to explore a wide range of topics—from love to ethics, from technology to equity—sparking deep conversations that strengthen interpersonal connections and promote a sense of belonging. The work of our group increases intercultural understanding, fosters critical thinking, and cultivates intellectual growth for our members. /p
 /p
Our mission is to provide participants from all backgrounds with the opportunity to enhance their debating and public speaking skills in Chinese languages. We achieve this through a diverse range of activities, including weekly training sessions, mock debates, group discussions, debate watch parties, domestic and international competitive tournaments (~3 major tournaments per year), and open house debate nights. The Student Association offers both a competitive team and a casual group, allowing members to engage at their preferred level of intensity, while encouraging involvement in both. Beyond debate, we prioritize the creation of a close-knit community, and work to foster meaningful connections. Social activities, such as shared meals following training sessions, debate watch parties, and open house debate nights, are integral to our approach. /p
 /p
In addition, we seek to engage with expert faculty and professionals through guest lectures and discussions, particularly on specialized topics, to further enrich our members' intellectual growth. Our overarching aim is to promote critical thinking, effective communication, and intercultural understanding by organizing and participating in debate events at various levels. /p
eligibility: Open to students across Harvard Griffin GSAS and other community members

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Soccer Club
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Soccer Club is dedicated to promoting fitness, wellness, and community among students through recreational and competitive soccer. The club organizes weekly practices, alongside social events such as World Cup watch parties and FIFA/EAFC video game tournaments. All activities are open to players of all skill levels. Our goal is to create an inclusive and welcoming environment where members can connect through a shared love of the game, build lasting friendships, and support one another in maintaining a healthy, balanced graduate student experience. When contacting the group leaders, please ensure that you leave your contact information, as we have no other way of replying to your message. PLEASE READ ME! If you'd like to join the WhatsApp group for pick up, please join the soccer club on Engage and then proceed to this link. Please ensure that your name matches on Engage and WhatsApp, as that is how we confirm admission in the group chat.
eligibility: Open to players of all skill levels

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Student Council
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Student Council (GSC) is the official representative body for students in the Harvard Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences at Harvard University. Through elected representatives and committee members, we advocate for, support, and recognize all Harvard Griffin GSAS students on all matters pertaining to their status as students of Harvard Griffin GSAS.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Student-Parents Group
description: The Harvard Griffin GSAS Student-Parents Group enriches the academic experience of and provides visibility and support to parents in Harvard Griffin GSAS (and across Harvard) and their families. A robust support system for student-parents and families helps create a caring and nurturing environment for the entire Harvard community, encourages and makes possible a healthy work-life balance for student-parents, and attracts a diverse, well-rounded, accomplished, and mature pool of graduate students.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Taiwan Student Association
description: Harvard Griffin GSAS Taiwan Student Association is a student organization dedicated to sharing a warmbr /and inclusive community of all of the Harvard Griffin GSAS students from Taiwan or interested inbr /the Taiwanese culture. Our main goals are to facilitate a smooth transition for students to thebr /school and life here in Boston, build a supportive community, and promote Taiwanese culturebr /within and outside of Harvard. Through a series of social, intellectual, and cultural events, such asbr /Lunar New Year Gala, Taiwanese language practice gathers and colloquium about the culture or socialbr /issues of Taiwan, we hope to promote lifelong friendships, provide a platform for exchange of ideas onbr /diverse issues, and share our culture with not only the Harvard Griffin GSAS but also the broaderbr /Harvard community./p

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Tennis Club
description: Since the summer of 2024, the Harvard Griffin GSAS Club Tennis has been fostering a vibrant community among members of Harvard graduate student community through a shared passion for tennis. Our club aims to create an engaging environment where tennis enthusiasts of all skill levels can connect and enjoy the sport.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS Women in Science and Engineering Group
description: The Harvard Graduate Women in Science and Engineering (HGWISE) is a Harvard Griffin GSAS graduate student organization founded in 2005 dedicated to the personal, academic, and professional development of women in natural sciences, social sciences, and engineering at Harvard University. HGWISE aims to enhance the graduate experience for all graduate students, and especially elevate the experience of female or women-identifying Harvard Griffin GSAS students in science and engineering at Harvard by providing opportunities for networking, professional development, and mentoring, as well as developing a meaningful community for all scientists.

name: Harvard Independent
description: As Harvard College's weekly undergraduate newsmagazine, the Harvard Independent’s purpose is to provide in‐depth, critical coverage of issues and events of interest to the Harvard community. The Independent has no political affiliation, instead offering diverse commentary on news, arts, sports, and student life.

name: Harvard Intercollegiate Model United Nations
description: ICMUN is concerned with educating Harvard students about international issues, the United Nations, and the skills of diplomacy and compromise by providing students the opportunity to participate as delegates in collegiate Model United Nations conferences.

name: Harvard Korean Association
description: Our central mission is to promote awareness about social, political, and cultural issues regarding Korea. All students are welcome to join— whether it is to find a tight-knit community, connect on the basis of Korean heritage, or simply learn more about different aspects of Korean culture.

name: Harvard Library
description: Harvard Library is a world-class academic library whose mission is to advance learning and research by engaging students and scholars in the creation and sharing of new knowledge. Our resources, services, and staff are accessible online, and we are available to support you remotely in your coursework and studies. We provide members of the Harvard community with access to extensive physical and digital resources, online subscriptions, and many of Harvard’s libraries offer a rich array of archival, manuscript, and rare book collections.

name: Harvard Medical and Dental School Coffee Association For Every Student (CAFES)
description: HMS/HSDM Coffee Association for Every Student (CAFES) is a student organization dedicated to building community and supporting local Boston cafes. Come join our regular Coffee and Connections events every semester to enjoy a free coffee/tea/treat on us.

name: Harvard Medical School - Office for Graduate Education (OGE)
description: The Office for Graduate Education provides a central resource to support the students enrolled in the HMS Master’s programs. The office works with students to explore ways to enhance or address aspects of the student experience and with program leadership to ensure that the needs of students are met, and relevant policies are developed, implemented, and clarified as needed. In the Office of Graduate Education (OGE), the Student Affairs (SA) team supports students’ personal, social, and academic development outside the classroom. The responsibilities of the OGE SA team include fostering an inclusive campus environment, coordinating student events and organizations, providing guidance and wellness resources, managing conduct matters, and promoting engagement, and community involvement. The team works to ensure students feel supported, connected, and empowered to succeed throughout their educational journey.
