Harvard Medical School Student Oncology Interest Group (Oncology IG)
Harvard Medical School Vascular Surgery Student Interest Group (HMS VSIG)
Harvard Medical School Women's Health Alliance (WomenHealth)
description: "Our mission is to advance women's health by empowering students to understand, analyze, and influence health policies. Our objectives include: fostering collaborations with the American Medical Association/Massachusetts Medical Society (AMA/MMS) and the other Harvard schools (e.g. Harvard Kennedy School, Harvard Law School); submitting policy proposals to the AMA/MMS to advance women's health; hosting workshops on policy writing and analysis; using op-eds and academic publications as tools for advocacy; showcasing careers in health policy; and building an extensive mentorship and research network that connects students to opportunities dedicated to advancing women's health at national and global levels.

name: Harvard Middle Eastern Cultural Association
description: The Harvard Middle Eastern Cultural Association (HMECA) seeks to foster a greater understanding and appreciation of Middle Eastern cultures by hosting and supporting various cultural, social, and academic programs within and surrounding the Harvard community. HMECA's primary goal is to serve as a social anchor and cornerstone for the interdisciplinary community of GSAS students, faculty, and interested members of the university to promote awareness of the region's history and culture, and to contribute to the social and intellectual vibrancy of Harvard University. HMECA will employ its resources to inform the Harvard community of the various programs it will be sponsoring.

name: Harvard Model Congress Europe
description: The mission of Harvard Model Congress Europe is to provide a platform for high school students from around the world to engage in constructive dialogue and debate on pressing global issues. We strive to cultivate critical thinking, leadership skills, and a deeper understanding of the complexities of international affairs among our participants. Through our simulated congressional committees, we aim to create a collaborative and inclusive environment where students can develop their public speaking, research, and negotiation abilities. We believe that by fostering empathy, intellectual curiosity, and an appreciation for diversity, we can inspire the next generation of leaders to make a positive impact in their communities and beyond.

name: Harvard Neuroscience Undergraduate Society
description: Bringing together Harvard neuroscience concentrators across tracks and classes to create community, explore research in neuroscience, and further scientific and interpersonal collaboration.

name: Harvard Opportunes
description: Founded in 1980, the Opportunes are Harvard's oldest (and boldest) all-gender a cappella group. With repertoire ranging from the pop anthems of Ariana Grande and Beyonce to the timeless classics of Stevie Wonder and Michael Jackson, the Opportunes are known for their energetic performances, intricate student arrangements, and award-winning discography.

name: Harvard Political Review
description: Founded in 1969, the Harvard Political Review (HPR) is an undergraduate-run journal of politics, policy, and culture. The review addresses domestic and international affairs, as well as political discourse on campus. It also conducts interviews with political figures and experts ranging from Alan Derschowitz to Anthony Fauci to Kara Swisher. The HPR features student perspectives in the form of articles, podcasts, investigations, and data-driven storytelling. Staff writers work closely with editors to strengthen pieces while maintaining their distinct journalistic voices. Aside from the standard publication route, students are encouraged to participate in a wide variety of programs including the Red Line Investigative Fellowship, the Summer Fellowship, and Columns. They can also pitch topic ideas for and contribute to our quarterly magazine. Previous issues include “Isolation” (Fall 2020), “Girls Girls Girls” (Winter 2019), “Engineering Earth” (Fall 2018), and “Body Politic” (Summer 2014).

name: Harvard Pops Orchestra
description: We, the members of the Harvard Pops Orchestra, endeavor to provide the Harvard community, the students, faculty, affiliates, and patrons thereof, with unique musical experiences. Through seasonal concerts built around creative themes, presenting an eclectic range of music from classical to jazz to rock, and employing theatrical and visual elements, we strive to create events that are not only enriching, but also highly enjoyable. In addition, we aim to cultivate the musical expertise of our musicians by scheduling regular rehearsals, as well as by encouraging students to conduct, arrange, orchestrate, or compose original works to be performed by the orchestra. Our overall goal is to play music at a very high level for the entertainment of the Harvard community.

name: Harvard Reserve Officer Training Corps Association
description: The (Harvard Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) Association) is concerned with providing institutional support and fostering camaraderie amongst Harvard College ROTC cadets and midshipmen of Air Force, Army, and Naval ROTC. Each year, the HROTC Association hosts a Welcome Back BBQ to welcome new cadets and midshipmen on campus. Throughout the year, we host a Visitas welcome, mentorship opportunities for current cadets and midshipmen, and a variety of events to build esprit de corps between branches. We also coordinate with the Harvard Undergraduate Veterans Organization to foster a spirit of military community on campus.

name: Harvard School of Dental Medicine Office of Student Affairs, Community & Campus Life
description: Student life at the Harvard School of Dental Medicine is enriched by the Office of Student Affairs, Community & Campus Life (OSACCL), which fosters a supportive and connected community to enhance the overall student experience. OSACCL is committed to creating a welcoming community where every student feels a sense of belonging, can grow as a leader, and is supported in their wellbeing and academic journey.

name: Harvard School of Dental Medicine Student AI Society
Harvard SEAS Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers
Harvard SEAS Society of Women Engineers (SWE)
Harvard Society of Black Scientists and Engineers
description: The Harvard Society of Black Scientists and Engineers seeks to support Black Harvard students pursuing degrees in life sciences, engineering, applied sciences, and other STEM fields. Our primary aim is to foster a sense of community among Black students in STEM at Harvard through offering academic and career advising, professional development workshops, help in the job and internship search, and various social events. We also seek to impact the wider Cambridge community by encouraging students to pursue STEM through mentoring and tutoring. Ultimately, we strive to combat underrepresentation in the sciences by facilitating the growth of black scientists at every level.

name: Harvard SoulFood Undergraduate Christian Fellowship
description: Harvard College SoulFood Christian Fellowship is a student group committed to demonstrating seeing Jesus’ hope and restoration coming to the Black Community at Harvard. We seek to nurture deep relationships with God and each other through community events, bible study, worship, and service in the Harvard community and beyond.

name: Harvard Swimming Club
description: Hey there! We are Harvard CSwim!

name: Harvard Taekwondo Club
description: As the largest martial arts club on campus, Harvard Taekwondo (HTKD) provides a uniquely vibrant environment for learning and training in the Olympic World Taekwondo (WT) style Taekwondo. Whether you are a beginner or a black belt, as a member, you will have the opportunity to grow and develop your skills under the guidance of our world-class masters and coaches.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Aerospace Collective
description: HUAC is dedicated to empowering Harvard undergraduates to participate in and meaningfully contribute to the field of aerospace and space exploration. The Collective achieves this mission through hands-on technical projects, structured programming, and access to industry professionals.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Alnisa's Medical Alliance
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Alnisa’s Medical Alliance strives to foster a community of support and positive encouragement for Muslim female pre-med students of Harvard College. Harvard Alnisa is concerned with offering a platform for Muslim females at Harvard College either interested in or pursuing the pre-medical pathway. We believe there is a real need to empower this community through providing resources and mentorship for their advancement on the pre-med track, promoting the values of Islam in their goals and aspirations as future physicians, providing education on issues related to women’s welfare and health, and building a genuine camaraderie among students identifying as a member of this community. This organization will also serve as a forum for students to address the challenges faced by the broader Muslim female physician community and serve as a space of solidarity. Appreciating the slowly changing demographics of physicians in the United States starts with uniting the Muslim female pre-med community on Harvard’s campus.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Alternative Investment Club
description: The Harvard Alternative Investment Club (HAI) is Harvard College’s first and only student organization dedicated to private equity, as well as other non-traditional investments. Visit our website to learn more!

name: Harvard Undergraduate Arts & Crafts Club
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Arts & Crafts Club was founded to create opportunities for students of all identities, disciplines, and artistic backgrounds to create, appreciate, and celebrate the arts. The ACC was founded by a group of sub-par (arguably terrible) artists of different disciplines, class years, and identities who share at least one thing in common: none of them have had any formal training in the arts. In fact, some feel that their talents never developed past finger-painting. The ACC firmly believes in the power of some good old arts & crafts, by bringing people together in a low-stakes, accessible, and fun setting.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Arts and Adventure Club
description: - Providing students with a welcoming, no comp, (truly!) no experience required club that is based in creativity - We hope to cultivate a community of people who are interested in trying something new - Get students off campus to explore the diversity of cultural offerings around Cambridge and Boston

name: Harvard Undergraduate Asian American Dance Troupe (AADT)
Harvard Undergraduate Asian Baptist Student Koinonia
Harvard Undergraduate Association for U.S. Cross-cultural Relations
Harvard Undergraduate Association of Ghanaian Students
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Association of Ghanaian Students is concerned with creating a close undergraduate community of Ghanaian students through the coordination of events and conversation that allows all members to feel valued, included, and empowered to succeed with the support of one another. Our organization was founded in the summer of 2022 when five students from Twi AB (Benista Owusu-Amo, Emma Mensah, Maame Forson, Verda Annan, and Yvonne Burke) came together to form what is now known as HUAGS. In our first year of operation, we hope to meet on a consistent basis, document all meetings/finances, plan at least two events per month, and ultimately connect all undergraduate Ghanaian-identifying students. We plan to host a Ghanaian Independence Day celebration annually. As we embark on this process, we hope to expand to include graduate students, more board positions, and outreach into the Cambridge community and beyond.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Astronomy Society
description: Create a welcoming atmosphere for Harvard undergraduates concentrating in astrophysics to learn more about the concentration and potential careers in the field.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Austrian-German Association
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Austrian German Association provides a welcoming and supportive space for students with a German educational or cultural background in order to share experiences of American culture and as Harvard students, including discussions of specific challenges associated with being a German Harvard College student, such as the transition from a German educational system to an American one. HUAGA thus focuses on welcoming Harvard freshmen and exchange students from German universities by providing them with a network of students who have gone through a similar process and on whom they can rely for advice and support in administrative, cultural, and social matters. The Association helps German students stay in touch with their home country by having a home community away from home, while fully involved in their life at Harvard. Additionally, the Association serves as a forum for discussion about German politics, current events, and the like. To fulfill this mission, HCGSA will hold welcoming events for newcomers at the beginning of the school year, pairing them with upperclassmen, as much as possible from a similar background, and familiarizing them with the broader Harvard campus and with Cambridge and Boston. Bi-weekly dinners will foster a sense of community and provide a supportive network for all members. We also aim to build a strong alumni network of German Harvard College graduates. HUAGA graduates could then help current college students plan for future academic and professional opportunities back in Germany or Europe in general. h as possible from a similar background, and familiarizing them with the broader Harvard campus and with Cambridge and Boston. Bi-weekly dinners will foster a sense of community and provide a supportive network for all members. We also aim to build a strong alumni network of German Harvard College graduates. HCGSA graduates could then help current college students plan for future academic and professional opportunities back in Germany or Europe in general.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Automotive Society
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Automotive Society is built around our Formula SAE team, where students design, build, and test a formula-style race car to compete in the annual FSAE competition. The competition includes static, dynamic, and presentation events that challenge students in engineering design, manufacturing, business strategy, and team communication. Our goal is to prepare undergraduates for careers in engineering and industry by giving them hands-on, team-based experience. Alongside our technical work, we host motorsport watch parties and community events to share our passion for the automotive world.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Beekeepers
description: We started with an idea in the Harvard Community Garden, but have since become an independent club. In the past, we have partnered with the Food Literacy Project to bring bees into the important farm to table picture, and the Health Advocacy Project with a small honey-tasting event. Since 2006, honeybee colonies in the US have seen collapse rates of up to 90%. As key pollinators, honeybees are directly responsible for cultivation of over 30% of the most important food crops. HUB seeks to stimulate active discussion on campus about not only the plight of the honeybee, but also to educate about the incredible world of apiculture. We would seek to bring together groups with important stakes in the fate of beekeeping. From all parts of the Harvard community, from the RoboBees Laboratory designing robots that mimic hive behavior at the School of Engineering & Applied Sciences, to the Environmental Exposure biologists working to link between declining bee health and pesticides at the School of Public Health.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Bhangra
description: Harvard Undergraduate Bhangra is concerned with meeting the artistic and cultural needs of students who express interest in the Punjabi dance form of Bhangra. Harvard Undergraduate Bhangra addresses this purpose through a variety of methods listed in its Constitution, and will hold auditions on times published on the official Instagram.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Biomedical Sciences Forum
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Biomedical Sciences Forum is dedicated to helping students build the skills to communicate scientific knowledge to audiences of all levels. The club hosts dynamic scientific presenters to discuss cutting-edge biomedical techniques with a focus on broadly applicable analytical thinking and fundamental principles. These events prepare students to understand and communicate future breakthroughs. Such skills are critical for undergraduates who will enter into scientific communities, science and technology policy arenas, as well as other fields. The club will host faculty members to demonstrate how fundamental scientific techniques and interdisciplinarity can advance diverse biological and medical fields. After hearing these presentations, members choose relevant peer-reviewed publications to present either individually or in groups at presentation dinners.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Birding Club
description: Our mission is to spark a love for birds in the Harvard undergraduate community! We'll be leading free birdwatching walks and hosting educational meetings and fun bird-related events.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Black Community Leaders
description: 1. The BCL should be responsible for making larger grander decisions for the community. 2. The BCL should promote collaboration to groups that appeal to the Black community at Harvard. The BCL should promote synergies rather than be a totalitarian governing body. 3. The BCL should foster neutrality in making big Black community decisions 4. The BCL should be a unified voice to outside the Black Community. There should be strength in numbers. The BCL should work together on initiatives of importance on campus.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Black Muslim Collective
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Black Muslim Collective is concerned with recognizing, honoring, and celebrating the unique experiences, struggles, and identities of Black Muslim students on campus. BMC works to shed light on the experiences of Black Muslim students as they navigate these multiple identities as well as create and foster a sense of community among those who hold these identities.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Black Premedical Society
description: Founded in 2019, the Harvard Undergraduate Black Pre-medical Society has strived to support Black students who have been historically underrepresented in the healthcare field. Given that only 5.7% of healthcare professionals in the United States are Black, many systemic barriers exclude disadvantaged populations from pursuing medical careers. This can have detrimental effects on our communities’ health, particularly for minority patients. HUBPS serves to create a space for mentorship, providing resources, and educating on healthcare disparities. Through our various programs and nurturing an inclusive environment, we aim to break down the barriers for Black pre-medical students.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Boardgame and Biosatellite Launch Enterprise
description: To provide a safe space for board game and snack enjoyers every Saturday night. Open to everyone whether they come once or every week.
eligibility: Open to everyone whether they come once or every week

name: Harvard Undergraduate Brazilian Association
description: The purpose of the Harvard Undergraduate Brazilian Association is to promote awareness about Brazilian culture at Harvard, as well as foster a community for students from and/or interested in Brazil throughout campus.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Breakers Organization
description: As the premier freestyle and street dance organization on campus, Harvard Breakers not only teaches students foundations in hip hop dance, but spreads awareness of hip hop culture and encourages engagement with the greater community. To promote greater engagement, the club organizes a semesterly jam that attracts dancers from New England and beyond. We do not limit membership based on background, ability, or previous experience. Anyone with an interest in street dance is welcome and encouraged to join.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Candela Latin Dance Troupe
description: Harvard Undergraduate Candela Latin Dance Troupe is a non-competitive performance dance group committed to celebrating and disseminating Latin culture through an array of genres. The group also seeks to bring awareness of Latin American culture to the greater Harvard and Boston communities.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Central Asian Students Association (HUCAS)
Harvard Undergraduate Chapter of Amnesty International
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Chapter of Amnesty International, a chapter of Amnesty International USA, is a student organization founded in 2023 that is dedicated to advancing human rights on Harvard University’s campus and beyond. We are committed to human rights advocacy through grassroots activism, organizing events, and directing campaigns that raise awareness and promote the basic human rights to justice, freedom, and truth.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Chapter of the Society for the Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science
Harvard Undergraduate Combat Robotics Club
description: The Harvard Undergraduate College Combat Robotics (HUCRC) exists to design, build, and compete with robots at the highest levels of national competition. We unite Harvard's most driven undergraduate engineers to push the boundaries of mechanical design, software innovation, and competitive excellence in the NHRL and beyond. Our mission is to: Compete in robotics, establishing Harvard as a dominant force in the national combat robotics arena Build a community of passionate engineers who embody grit, ingenuity, and an unwavering commitment to execution Develop technical skills through hands-on experience in mechanical design, fabrication, electronics, and software engineering Foster a culture of excellence where hard work, creative problem-solving, and getting things done are paramount Create opportunities for undergraduates to apply classroom knowledge to real-world engineering challenges under intense competitive pressure Represent Harvard with distinction in the growing field of combat robotics, inspiring the next generation of engineers and innovators

name: Harvard Undergraduate Consulting on Business and the Environment
Harvard Undergraduate Creative Writing Collective
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Creative Writing Collective is concerned with filling the gap in the creative writing community on Harvard’s campus. Through mentorship, drop-in hours, networking events, book clubs, workshop events, speaker series, and service opportunities, we ultimately seek to create a radically inclusive, tight-knit community for writers of all kinds on campus (& beyond), by: • Providing support and accountability for writers working on projects • Connecting writers with publishers, nonprofits, grants, and each other • Organizing writing & non-writing related events & programming • Partnering with other creative orgs at Harvard • Serving the greater Boston community

name: Harvard Undergraduate Crimson Cellos
description: The mission of the Harvard Undergraduate Crimson Cellos is to foster a vibrant community of cellists by establishing Harvard's premier cello ensemble. Crimson Cellos aims to spread musical diffusion by challenging cello misconceptions, which include its believed ability to play only classical music and role as a relatively less prominent instrument in the orchestra. Our ensemble enriches both the Harvard campus and the greater Boston area through rehearsals, jam sessions, and performances at venues like Arts First, the Harvard Art Museum, and local hospitals. Additionally, we host speaker events and educational opportunities to inspire others to pursue music and encourage deeper engagement with this beautiful instrument.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Czech and Slovak Club
description: The Czech and Slovak Club at Harvard College aims to foster a vibrant and diverse community for students, alumni, and faculty with an interest in the culture, history, and heritage of Czechia and Slovakia. Through cultural events and community outreach, we seek to promote understanding and appreciation of the shared traditions and modern developments of both nations.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Dominican Student Association
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Dominican Student Association is a cultural organization created to celebrate the Dominican and Dominican-American experience. We seek to provide students who are Dominican-identifying and those who want to learn about Dominican culture with a safe space to feel both represented and welcome. As an organization, we emphasize the inclusion of all identities and want everyone on campus to feel comfortable thriving in the space that’s provided by DSA. Through our various branches, we emphasize the importance of providing members with a safe social space, establishing professional networks to connect members to Dominican professionals and alumni, and of giving back to the Dominican community outside of campus.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Ethics Society
description: Our goal is to encourage collaborative and accessible discourse on pressing ethical issues and to supply students and the wider public with an ethical toolkit that they can productively apply to their daily lives.

name: Harvard Undergraduate European Initiative
description: The Harvard Undergraduate European Initiative seeks to create a space to discuss and learn about European politics, history, and culture at Harvard College. Through its events, HUEI strives to create a vibrant community for all students interested in Europe. At the same time, HUEI seeks to foster a sense of community among international students heading to Harvard from European countries—especially those from under-represented countries.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Faith and Action
description: The purpose of Harvard Undergraduate Faith and Action, by God’s grace and power, is to create an environment that develops and nurtures mature Christian leaders for every sector of society. The group will seek to promote greater awareness and understanding of the Holy Bible and the Christian faith in the Harvard community by appropriate means such as speakers, Bible courses, Bible studies, retreats, book discussions, leadership training, community service, fellowship, and other activities. It also seeks to serve as an authentic Christian witness to the Harvard community, expressing the Good News of Jesus Christ, as set forth in the Holy Bible, through all of its activities and challenging Christians to develop a Biblical worldview and to live lives of increasing faithfulness to Jesus Christ.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Federal Reserve Challenge
description: The Harvard Fed Challenge Team is a small, tight-knit group on campus that analyzes macroeconomic conditions, formulates monetary policy recommendations, and presents them to leading economists at the Boston Fed and at the Board of Governors in Washington D.C. as part of the National College Federal Reserve Challenge.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Forensic Speech
description: The mission of Harvard College Forensic Speech is to equip undergraduate students in becoming public speakers, educators, and presenters about a wide variety of topics, while providing a venue to compete and share their voices with larger audiences.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Friends of Médecins Sans Frontières (FoMSF)
Harvard Undergraduate Game Developers
description: We are a student-run organization dedicated to the learning and practice of video game development.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Gender Inclusivity in Mathematics
Harvard Undergraduate Global Alliance for Medical Innovation
Harvard Undergraduate Half Asian People's Association
description: Our mission is to celebrate, empower, and unite individuals of mixed Asian heritage by providing a supportive community that embraces and promotes cultural diversity, identity exploration, and education. We aim to foster a sense of belonging, understanding, and pride among our members, while also advocating for awareness, inclusivity, and representation in the broader community.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Hawai'i Club
description: Harvard Undergraduate Hawaii Club aims to serve both the community of Hawaiian students attending Harvard College and the general student community at large by practicing and promoting the unique island culture on campus.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Hellenic Society
description: At the heart of our society lies a profound respect and passion for the rich heritage of Greece. We aim to foster a deeper understanding and appreciation of Hellenic culture among the Harvard community. Through our activities, we seek to create a welcoming space for students of Hellenic descent and those interested in the Hellenic world, fostering connections, dialogue, and cultural exchange.

name: Harvard Undergraduate International Genetically Engineered Machines (iGEM)
description: As Harvard College iGEM (International Genetically Engineered Machine), we seek to establish a community of creative synthetic biologists from a variety of concentrations and disciplines. Our work each year will culminate in our participation in the iGEM competition where we will share our projects with an international audience, connect with other teams of synthetic biologists, relevant companies, and organizations.

name: Harvard Undergraduate International Relations on Campus
Harvard Undergraduate Italian Society
description: The mission of an Italian Society is to promote an appreciation and understanding of Italian culture, language, and heritage among its members and the wider community. Through a range of cultural, educational, and social activities, the Italian Society aims to foster a deeper understanding of the rich history, traditions, and art of Italy, as well as the contemporary Italian society and its contributions to the world. The Italian Society also seeks to provide opportunities for language learning and proficiency in Italian, as well as opportunities for members to connect with one another and build lifelong friendships based on a shared passion for Italian culture. Ultimately, the Italian Society strives to inspire its members to become global citizens who are committed to promoting cross-cultural understanding and making a positive impact in their communities.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Japan Society
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Japan Society celebrates the Japanese community and its presence on campus. From hosting monthly social events to expanding the network beyond Harvard College, we strive to give opportunities for students of Japanese and non-Japanese backgrounds to connect over our culture.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Knitting Circle
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Knitting Circle is concerned with bringing undergraduate fiber arts together within a relaxed environment. We provide undergrads from all class years, backgrounds, and experiences a space to come together around the fiber arts and build new friendships. Additionally, we aim to serve the greater community through the fiber arts. Each year, knitting circle members will organize a donation drive to a charity, such as a homeless shelter or animal welfare organization. Members will be encouraged to make items including blankets, hats, or mittens to donate to those in need.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Latina Empowerment and Development
Harvard Undergraduate Latines in Health Careers
Harvard Undergraduate Latinxs in Finance & Technology
Harvard Undergraduate Lifestyle Medicine Interest Group
Harvard Undergraduate LowKeys
description: Founded in 1999, we are one of Harvard's award-winning, contemporary co-ed a cappella group. We perform shows twice a year in Harvard’s historic Sanders Theatre, embark on world tours, and sing upon request at venues in and outside Greater Boston. Our members hail from all around the globe and from diverse academic backgrounds, but we are united by our dedication to the group and our love for a cappella. All songs we perform are selected and arranged by current and past members of the group. As a result, we sing music from a wide variety of genres, ranging from classic rock and hip-hop to top 40, R&B, jazz and everything in between.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Mission: Brain Chapter
description: Our chapter aims to promote awareness, education, and engagement in neurosurgical care, particularly in underserved communities. We will work in collaboration with Harvard Medical School Mission:Brain and alongside medical professionals to provide outreach, advocacy, and educational opportunities related to global health and neurosurgery. The chapter will bridge gaps in healthcare access worldwide by supporting neurosurgical initiatives globally and helping connect students and professionals with resources and events.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Mock Trial Association
description: The Harvard College Mock Trial Association is dedicated to furthering a passion for trial advocacy and the law at Harvard College. We are a student-run group which competes regionally and nationally in competitions organized by the American Mock Trial Association. These competitions consist of trying legal cases in front of real judges and attorneys. We seek to enhance and apply its members' acute analytical reasoning, strategic thinking and rhetorical skills.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Music Business Association (HUMBA)
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Music Business Association (HUMBA) is a student-led organization dedicated to exploring the diverse facets of the music industry through interactive workshops, speaker events featuring industry professionals, industry trips, an annual conference, and networking opportunities

name: Harvard Undergraduate Music In Hospitals and Nursing Homes Using Entertainment as Therapy
Harvard Undergraduate Negotiation Club
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Negotiation Club is dedicated to educating and empowering students in the art of negotiation. Our mission is to provide comprehensive training in principled negotiation methods and practical techniques, enabling members to become skilled negotiators in both their professional and personal lives.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Network of Enlightened Women (NeW)
description: The Network of Enlightened Women educates, equips, and empowers women to be principled leaders for a free society. Educate – NeW educates women on campus and early in their careers on the principles of freedom and opportunity by hosting speakers, holding debates, and providing intellectual resources. In its education work, NeW serves as a thought leader, promoting independent thinking and providing intellectual diversity on college campuses and in public discussions on women, policy, and culture. Equip – NeW trains pro-liberty women to serve as leaders through campus sessions, national conferences, leadership retreats, and professional development programs. Empower – NeW cultivates a vibrant community of women through campus chapters, professional chapters, and our online presence that emboldens participants to confidently advocate for pro-liberty ideas in their schools, workplaces, homes, and communities. NeW also connects program participants with career-advancing professional opportunities.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Nordic Club
description: Harvard Undergraduate Nordic Club is dedicated to fostering a community for Nordic students at Harvard University. The mission of the organization is to gather students with a shared background as well as preserve cultural traditions that these students share; these may include events ranging from informal social gatherings to the celebration of national holidays. Harvard Undergraduate Nordic Club will benefit the Harvard community by creating an inclusive and accepting space for incoming, current and former Nordic students of Harvard University.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Partners in Health Engage
description: Harvard Undergraduate Partners in Health Engage advances global health equity through advocacy, fundraising, and community building efforts. We directly improve global health outcomes through sustainable solutions founded upon cultural competency.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Photography Club
description: The goal of the Harvard Undergraduate Photography Club is to provide student photographers with the resources and artistic community they require to develop and grow their photographic skills. This community will give students inspiration and instruction through interaction with their fellow photographers and will help advance the visual arts on the Harvard campus.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Plant Based
description: Harvard Undergraduate Plant Based is a student-led organization broadly focused on accelerating the transition to plant-centric food systems at the intersection of social justice, public health, environmental sustainability, and animal welfare. We hope to educate and empower the next generation of leaders to bring about a more ethical, sustainable, healthy, accessible, culturally appropriate, and efficient plant-centric food system. The purpose of this organization is to create a space for students to learn about and partake in the transition to sustainable food systems. We aim to advance these goals using the following levers: - Influencing federal, state, and local policies and initiatives - Creating a plant-based community at the collegiate level and using this to effect change to food practices in university dining halls - Generating mainstream attention on plant-based solutions through media coverage, campaigns, and outreach - Collaborating with other student groups, non-governmental organizations, activists, and experts - Incorporating relevant food systems issues into our events and initiatives, ie. food desserts, food justice, equity, and accessibility

name: Harvard Undergraduate Poker Club
description: The Harvard Poker Club is concerned with the development of quantitative, analytical and perceptive skills acquired through the play and study of poker. We will educate the Harvard community on how card game playing can sharpen many important real-life skills in addition to being an enjoyable pastime, and through doing so build a community for poker enthusiasts on Harvard’s campus.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Pre-Dental Society
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Pre-Dental Society is committed to providing interested students with the information and opportunities necessary for succeeding in the pre-dental / oral health community on campus.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Pre-Veterinary Society
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Pre-Veterinary Society is concerned with promoting and stimulating interest in the veterinary sciences for interested students seeking to pursue or explore the field of veterinary medicine.

name: Harvard undergraduate Premedical Society for International Students
Harvard Undergraduate Puzzle Club
description: The purpose of Harvard Undergraduate Puzzle Club is to create an inclusive, active community for puzzle solving among Harvard students. HUPC aims to encourage collaboration among puzzle enthusiasts at the College.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Quantitative Traders
description: The mission of the Harvard Undergraduate Quantitative Traders (HUQT) is to foster an educational and supportive community which, through mentorship and projects, prepares students for careers in quantitative finance. HUQT is comprised of many of Harvard’s brightest statistics, math, and computer science students. Our members are selected through a rigorous interview process and go on to intern and work full-time at the world’s leading quantitative hedge funds and market-makers, including Jane Street, Two Sigma, Citadel, HRT, Jump Trading, SIG, Optiver, IMC Trading, and more.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Quantum Computing Association
description: Our mission is to engage undergraduate students from any and all backgrounds in quantum computing. We aim to connect our members to faculty, researchers, and industry leaders from Harvard and beyond to help them learn more about quantum information and quantum computation, to expose them to research opportunities, and to build a diverse community of students exploring the quantum revolution.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Queer Advocates
description: Our mission is to advocate for the well-being of Queer students both on Harvard's campus and in the greater Massachusetts area as well as to educate students on Queer policy and teach them how to effectively narrate their stories to foster change.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Rare Diseases
description: Harvard Undergraduate Rare Diseases (HURD) is a student organization committed to raising awareness of rare diseases and creating a space for productive collaboration between patients, caregivers, researchers, physicians, and students. Our organization has both social and academic components, as we seek to foster dialogue between the Harvard community and the broader rare disease community, while also empowering students to contribute to solutions through education, research, and innovation. The signature event of HURD is the annual rare disease hackathon, HackRare. Held in honor of Rare Disease Day® (February 28/29), HackRare convenes the aforementioned groups to highlight rare disease challenges and develop computational and scientific solutions to real-world problems. Beyond HackRare, HURD members participate in discussions, conferences, and outreach events to connect students with opportunities in rare disease research and advocacy. By cultivating partnerships across disciplines and communities, HURD enriches Harvard’s campus with a culture of empathy, innovation, and service, driving progress toward a future where the needs of all diseases can be met.

Science Club for Girls at Harvard College will work to create a community of Harvard undergraduate and graduate students dedicated to serving local Cambridge and Boston schools and generating enthusiasm for science through after school and extracurricular activities. Science Club for Girls at Harvard College fulfills a need at Harvard College for a volunteering opportunity that empowers future women scientists, and it fulfills a need of the Cambridge community for free and educational after school opportunities.

By fostering a sense of camaraderie and mutual interest, we hope to enhance the college experience for all members through shared enjoyment and discussion.

We focus on education through practice, with students participating in active consulting projects with startups and developing public equity research presentations with potential to deploy real capital.

description: The Harvard Undergraduate Texas Club is a welcoming community for students from Texas and the broader South, as well as anyone who feels connected to Southern culture. We are a low-commitment organization with no application, no comp, and no fees, designed to be a space to step away from the stress of campus life. Our goal is to offer a positive and thoughtful perception of the South in the Northeast and to use the resources available at Harvard to support progress in our home communities.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Think Tank
description: We are a student-run research collective that aims to bridge the gap between academia and advocacy. We want to use the vast and uniquely valuable academic resources at our disposal, including world-class professors, networks of experts, and highly-accomplished students to tackle some of the world’s most pressing issues. With that spirit in mind, we have chosen two research focuses in the realm of climate change and American leadership legitimacy through coordinated domestic and foreign policy.

description: The mission of Harvard Undergraduate Tuesday Magazine is to publish creative writing and art by Harvard University students and foster a democratic and inclusive literary arts community. The magazine is a vehicle through which both Harvard and non-Harvard communities can enjoy and celebrate the creative work of Harvard students. Community events allow the community to bond and grow over a shared interest in literature, art, publishing, and the creative practice.

name: Harvard Undergraduate UNICEF Club
description: The Harvard Undergraduate UNICEF Club, a student-run organization at Harvard College, is concerned with the humanitarian aid of children across the globe. Through various events and activities, we aim to support UNICEF in their goal to provide health care and immunizations, safe water and sanitation, nutrition, education, emergency relief, and more necessities to children.

name: Harvard Undergraduate Veritas Forum
description: The Harvard Undergraduate Veritas Forum (‘Organization’) is concerned with asking and answering some of life’s hardest questions alongside fellow students, faculty, and experts. With a commitment to courageous discourse, this Organization puts the historic Christian faith in dialogue with other religious, ethical, and spiritual worldviews and invites participants from all backgrounds to confront difficult questions together. In doing so, this organization aims to create a space that seriously considers and lives out the original motto of Harvard University: “Veritas Christo et Ecclesiae,” in English “Truth for Christ and the Church.”

We also advocate for students and postdocs within the department on a range of issues. We are always looking for volunteers to help manage these events and activities, and we welcome any input on how to improve student and postdoc life in the Department. Contact any of the board members or come to our monthly GPC meetings to get involved!

name: Harvard University Health Services
description: Harvard University Health Services is a multi-specialty medical practice dedicated to caring for members of the Harvard community — students, faculty, staff, retirees, and their dependents. Our mission is to nurture the health of the Harvard community through compassionate delivery of high-quality, equitable care and advancement of overall wellbeing. To Heal. To Care. To Educate.

We are dedicated to outreach to the local community to promote awareness of women in chemistry. We also strive to promote equity and inclusion, particularly for gender-based issues, in the Harvard Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology. We are committed to promoting all peoples in STEM that identify as women, of all races, religions, disability and sexual orientation.

name: Harvard World Model United Nations
description: The purposes of this organization shall be: (1) to provide college and university students throughout the world with a conference that authentically simulates the workings of specified committees and specialized agencies of the United Nations; (2) to foster an understanding of the intricacies of international negotiation by encouraging active participation of students as United Nations delegates; (3) to provide Harvard students with an opportunity, which they may not have otherwise, to travel abroad and meet their peers from foreign nations and cultures in a common forum; (4) to promote a general awareness at Harvard of the growing importance of the United Nations as an arbiter of international conflicts; and (5) to distinguish Harvard as an institution concerned with educating the international community on the United Nations.

description: The Hasty Pudding Institute of 1770’s philanthropic mission is to provide educational and developmental support in all aspects of the performing arts for the underprivileged, to encourage satire and comedy, and to cultivate young talent around the world.

name: HBS Show
description: The rumors are true...The HBS Show Club is the number one community on campus! A (non-exhaustive) list of reasons: Annual Events Most anticipated events of the year: The HBS Show is a full length, original parody musical entirely written, produced, directed performed, and designed by and for HBS students. Cabaret is a satirical variety set-list of singing, dancing, and stand-up comedy, all designed to lovingly poke fun at HBS. Storied History: What started in 1974 with a sketch show and one spotlight has grown to three massive, sold out performances in Klarman Hall. Students, faculty, staff, and alumni all pack the house every year for one of the most celebrated traditions at Harvard Business School. Unleash Your Latest Creativity and Join the Most Fun Community on Campus: With songs from ranging genres (pop, classic rock, Broadway, Disney, and more), the community offers space to be the rock/pop/Broadway star you've always dreamed to be! All levels welcome and no previous experience required. Performing opportunities range from song, comedy, dance, and orchestra. If you'd rather be behind the scenes, no problem! Think you're funny? Join the writing staff. Have a vision? Like to be in charge? Join directing or production. Interested in costumes or tech? Be a show designer. There are endless opportunities to get involved and express yourself! Every single member of our community is essential to our success. Feel free to reach out and learn more!

Topics to be covered within the club include fitness and movement, workplace wellness, healthy eating, nutrition, mind-body connection, preventative and personalized medicine, personal care, clean beauty and anti-aging. description: The Harvard Medical School Nutrition Student Interest Group (NSIG) is dedicated to advancing nutrition education, research, and clinical practice within medical training. NSIG introduces students to the foundational and emerging roles of nutrition in disease prevention, health promotion, and the management of acute and chronic illness across specialties. Through expert talks, culinary medicine and counseling workshops, case-based discussions, and mentorship opportunities, NSIG equips students with practical skills to integrate evidence-based nutrition into patient care. The group also highlights career pathways in clinical nutrition, public health, endocrinology, gastroenterology, obesity medicine, and academic research, while fostering collaboration with dietitians, physicians, and interdisciplinary partners. NSIG welcomes students at all stages of training—from those newly interested in nutrition science to those pursuing scholarship or leadership in the field—and aims to build a community committed to improving health through nutrition-informed medical care.

Our mission is to increase awareness of the breadth, diversity, and professional fulfillment offered by careers in pediatric medicine.

name: HMS Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) Student Interest Group
description: The mission of the HMS PM&R Interest Group is to educate medical students about the unique and impactful field of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, foster meaningful connections with PM&R physicians and residents, and provide service opportunities that embody the specialty's core principles of restoring function and improving quality of life for individuals with disabilities and chronic conditions.

description: The Harvard Medical School Radiation Oncology Interest Group (ROIG) is dedicated to introducing medical students to the field of radiation oncology and the multidisciplinary care of patients with cancer. ROIG provides opportunities to explore the science, technology, and clinical practice of radiation therapy, including emerging innovations in image-guided treatment, stereotactic techniques, brachytherapy, and combined modality care. Through faculty talks, resident panels, skills workshops, and mentorship connections, ROIG supports students interested in oncology, medical technology, physics, and patient-centered cancer care. The group also highlights career pathways in radiation oncology and fosters collaboration with related specialties such as medical oncology, surgical oncology, radiology, and biomedical engineering. ROIG welcomes students at all stages of training—from those newly curious about oncology to those pursuing research or careers in the field—and aims to build an inclusive community committed to advancing cancer treatment and improving patient outcomes.

description: The HMS/HSDM Health Policy Society exists to give medical and dental students a structured home for learning, practicing, and leading in health policy. Our objectives are to: (1) build core policy skills through workshops on topics such as legislation, regulation, financing, and advocacy; (2) host speaker events that connect students with policymakers, practitioners, and researchers working at local, national, and global levels; (3) create cross-school partnerships and pathways for mentorship, research, and summer opportunities; and (4) coordinate student-led projects that translate policy ideas into tangible impact for patients and communities.

Through workshops, mentorship, and collaborative projects, we foster a supportive community that helps students build marketable skills, pursue passion-driven ventures, and create long-term financial stability while balancing academic and clinical commitments.

name: HMS/HSDM Students for Environmental Advocacy in Medicine (SEAM)
description: HMS SEAM (Students for Environmental Advocacy in Medicine) aims to engage medical and dental students at HMS/HSDM around increasing awareness of the impacts of climate change on human health. Our advocacy initiatives involve a variety of projects relating to climate action; a few examples of projects include expanding composting at HMS, supporting institutional decarbonization efforts, supporting the work of local environmental justice groups, and volunteering for legislative campaigns to advance renewable energy. Our educational arm seeks to further integrate climate and health into the medical curriculum. We also serve as a nexus for students interested in connecting with HMS faculty engaged in research and advocacy in the fields of climate and health, planetary health, and environmental health.

name: HMS/HSDM Teddy Bear Clinic (Teddy)
description: HMS/HSDM Teddy Bear Clinic is a community outreach initiative for elementary school students to experience medical scenarios by using stuffed animals/action figures as patients. By caring for their stuffed animals, our goal is to help children learn to trust healthcare providers and become less anxious about future medical visits, while also learning basic health concepts. We hope these experiences reinforce the importance of primary care in the children's households and cultivate their interest in pursuing healthcare careers. It also provides an opportunity for medical students to practice their trauma-informed care, patient-friendly language, and physical exam techniques.

description: Students for Smiles at the Harvard School of Dental Medicine is a student-run outreach group focused on improving oral health literacy and access across Greater Boston. The organization delivers hands-on education and distributes essential hygiene supplies in community centers, senior centers, public libraries, K–8 schools, and local food pantries.

name: HSDM/HMS Student 3D Maker Club (3D)
description: Our mission is to build a collaborative community of makers, innovators, and future clinicians who use 3D printing to advance healthcare and explore creative hobbies. We bring together dental and medical students to prototype clinical solutions, design teaching models, and also encourage personal projects that spark curiosity and joy. By offering workshops, open build nights, and mentorship from clinicians, researchers, and industry experts, we aim to spark curiosity and innovation, bridge engineering with clinical practice, and build a culture of creativity and collaboration that enriches both student life and patient care.

name: Human Biology, Behavior, and Evolution Club
Human Rights and Business Student Association
description: The Harvard Law School Human Rights and Business Association (HuB) brings together students who have an interest in the continuously developing field of business and human rights, corporate responsibility and accountability. The organization engages students from all Harvard schools and other universities in the greater Boston area in events, workshops and seminars, and provides a space where students can learn more about the field, network with experts, as well as explore future career opportunities.

description: The Harvard Law School In Vino Veritas serves to introduce interested members of the Harvard Law School community to the exciting world of wine at formal tastings, informal blind tasting workshops, and tasting dinners at area restaurants.

name: Indigo Peer Counseling
description: Peer counseling is a service for Harvard undergrads to use when they need to need process concerns or experiences to another person, and it’s in a confidential setting. Indigo strives to foster a supportive and compassionate campus for undergraduate students grappling with and addressing issues of race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, first generation, immigration status, and other identity concerns at Harvard College. Indigo provides confidential non-directive, non-judgmental, peer counseling as well as informational resources for students. We seek to support students of all racial and socioeconomic backgrounds and help create an open and welcoming campus climate based on respect of all students.

name: Institute of Politics
description: Established as a memorial to President John F. Kennedy, the IOP’s mission is to unite and engage students, particularly undergraduates, with academics, politicians, activists, and policymakers on a non-partisan basis to inspire them to consider careers in politics and public service. Through our sixteen programs, internships, and conferences, the IOP offers wide-ranging opportunities for students to practice, get inspired, and gain the skills for a future in public service.

name: Intellectual Property Law Association
description: The Harvard Law School Intellectual Property Law Association (IPLA) is an active community for Harvard Law School students to explore their interests in intellectual property, including patent, copyright, trademark, and trade secrets. IPLA is a space for HLS students to connect with employers in the intellectual property law space, learn about new developments from distinguished practitioners and academics, gain from networking and professional training sessions, and build community among students interested in intellectual property law at HLS.

name: Intellectual, Cultural, and Literary - Student Center Fellows
description: Here at Harvard Griffin GSAS, we're all intellectual, cultural, and literary! And as your Intellectual, Cultural, and Literary Fellows at the Student Center, we're here to provide you with additional activities to enrich your Harvard experience. Through film screenings, faculty dinners and other activities, we hope to foster discussions that fuel our ongoing quest for intellectual growth and learn more about our different cultural customs and ways of knowing. We offer book clubs, creative writing workshops, film screenings, poetry and songwriting nights, as well as discussion groups, and study bootcamps. We also publish The Graduate Review, an annual journal featuring writing and artwork by Harvard Griffin GSAS students. Above all, we hope to provide you with forums in which you can continue to stay engaged with peers and invited speakers beyond the walls of your seminar room, department, or lab.

name: Interdisciplinary Discussion on Disease and Health, a Harvard Griffin GSAS Student Group
description: The mission of Interdisciplinary Discussion on Disease and Health, a Harvard Griffin GSAS Student Group (IDDH-HGG), is to create a platform for students at Harvard Griffin GSAS to engage in interdisciplinary discussions outside the classroom or a single department on disease-related topics. In each discussion, one disease topic will be chosen, and we will actively reach out to students working on the topic to present their work. These students may major in different fields, including medicine, public health, basic biological science research, and engineering. They would gather and share their own work to assist each other in understanding how they attempt to address the targeted disease topic. Our club stands out in two ways. Firstly, we strive to create awareness about collaboration in science and form a community of students who are passionate about pursuing a scientific career, honing their scientific and professional communication skills, and sharing knowledge across different domains. Secondly, our discussions revolve around diseases. Students are encouraged to share the translational side of their knowledge and graduate work related to diseases. We provide opportunities for members to present their topics of interest in both informal discussions and formal presentations. The target audience of IDDH-HGG is primarily students at Harvard Griffin GSAS, but it can extend to diverse audiences, including high school students, established researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders.

name: International Arbitration Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School International Arbitration Law Students Association ( HIALSA) dedicates exclusively to promote international arbitration! A group of Harvard Law School students, passionate about international arbitration, proposed to the Board of Students the creation of HIALSA to offer a forum for students to learn about and discuss emerging topics in international arbitration and to develop connections between students and successful practitioners.

name: InTouch
description: We are graduate students within SEAS here to support our peers concerning all aspects of student life. Peer staffers are trained to listen, brainstorm, and if necessary direct you to additional resources within and outside Harvard.

name: Investment Club
description: To improve members' understanding of investment management; to help members develop practical investment skills and test them in the markets; and to create superior access to career opportunities in the investment industry. description: The Islamic Society provides an open, inclusive environment to HBS Muslims while actively engaging the larger HBS community on issues related to Islam. name: JD/MBA Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School JD/MBA Students Association ( JD/MBA) supports JD/MBA students with job applications and interviews, organize events on topics impacting business and the law, and schedule treks to visit law firms, investment firms and innovative companies.

name: JD/MPP Joint Degree Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School JD/MPP Joint Degree Law Students Association ( JD/MPP) supports and encourages students seeking an interdisciplinary education in government, public policy, and law, and prepares them for leadership positions in public service.

name: Jessup Moot Court
description: The Harvard Law School Jessup Moot Court Team competes annually in the Philip C. Jessup International Law Moot Court Competition, the world’s largest and most prestigious moot court competition first held at Harvard in 1960. Today, the Jessup draws law students from over 100 countries and jurisdictions, with each team presenting arguments as part of a fictional dispute between states before the International Court of Justice. Participants prepare written and oral pleadings to address timely issues of public international law, arguing both the applicant and respondent positions of the case before a panel of judges. Our team consists of four oralists and one of counsel each year, and tryouts for the positions are held in the fall. 1Ls, 2Ls and 3Ls interested in the practice of international law are encouraged to apply. The team also works closely with LLMs, so please reach out if you have prior experience with the Competition.

name: Jewish Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Jewish Law Students Association (JLSA) is the affinity group for Jewish law students at Harvard Law School, running social, educational, cultural, and religious programming for all Jewish law students regardless of background or affiliation.

name: Jewish Students Association
description: To serve as a resource to develop, inform, support, and enrich the Jewish community on campus. Our goals are to encourage student participation in Jewish events, build stronger ties among Jewish students and nearby Jewish organizations, and foster a sense of community. Annual Events Student Retreat Holiday Dinners Speaker Series Middle East Rapprochement

Justice For Palestine
description: The Harvard Law School Justice for Palestine (JFP) is a student group founded in 2000 after the start of the second Intifada in the Occupied Palestinian Territories. JFP is a community of HLS students concerned about the lack of campus-wide debate about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the at large misperceptions of the fundamental issues related to Palestine. JFP is committed to a secular, humanist, and legalistic approach to dialogue about Israel/Palestine and seeks to advocate the rights of the Palestinian people.

name: Kesem Harvard Undergraduate
description: Camp Kesem Harvard Undergraduate is committed to creating a world where every child who has a parent with a cancer diagnosis or has lost a parent to cancer is never alone. We support these children through and beyond their parent's cancer by offering free, fun-filled summer camp and year-round programming.

name: Kidney Disease Screening and Awareness Program
Korean Association of Harvard Law School
description: The Korean Association of Harvard Law School (KAHLS) is a network of Korean students at Harvard Law. The organization’s goal is to develop a bond among the Korean JDs and LLMs and to function as a bridge between HLS and the larger, university-wide Korean community. It also provides information on events and news of the Harvard community that may be of particular interest to Korean students. Most of all, we are a close bunch and a good group of friends!

name: La Alianza at Harvard Law School
description: La Alianza at Harvard Law School (La Alianza) is an organization dedicated to providing support to Latino/a students at Harvard Law School and increasing understanding of the issues that face Latinos in the United States. La Alianza provides academic and career placement assistance for its members.

name: Labor and Employment Action Project at Harvard Law School
description: The Harvard Law School Labor and Employment Action Project ( LEAP) is an organization of students interested in labor and employment issues. We feel that the power of working people to organize themselves has become more, not less, essential in today’s changing economy, and undertake to explore and support such organization. Therefore, our activities include both education of ourselves and our community on labor and employment issues, and activism where we see a need to lend our voices to local or national struggles.

name: Lambda
description: The Harvard Law School Lambda ( HLS Lambda) is a community of lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans*, queer and allied students at Harvard Law School. As a social and political student organization, Lambda provides programming and events to serve LGBTQ students and allies at HLS. Lambda also plays an active role in the LGBTQ rights movement by organizing and sponsoring conferences, networking with national LGBTQ rights leaders, and connecting students with research and academic opportunities and activism related to gender and sexuality.

name: LatAm Club
description: The LatAm Club offers a strong and engaging community of Harvard Business School students and partners that share an interest in Latin America. The club aims to represent Latin America region on campus, promote Latin American business and culture, and identify career opportunities for MBA students. Annual Events Latin American Conference Fall Retreat to Cape Cod & Spring Ski Retreat Back to School Gatsby Party Christmas Party with HBS employees Latam Welcome BBQ Latin America recruiting opportunities and speakers
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Latinas Unidas de Harvard College
description: Latinas Unidas shall be the materialization of a vision: the unification of Harvard College students who have a passion for and/or interest in the lives of Latina women. LU provides a forum for community building, intellectual discussion, and the empowerment of women. We believe that our individual backgrounds, while diverse, combine to form a strong and unique culture. We foster this strength and unity through three main branches of action: 1) Advocacy Events 2) Social Events and 3) Professional Outreach. We believe and embrace the important responsibility to the Latinx and greater Latin American community to showcase the power of women, build communal ties, and establish long-lasting career pipelines.

name: Latino Student Organization
description: LASO’s mission is to promote and support Harvard Business School’s Latinx students. Representing a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, interests, and Latinx heritage, LASO members spearhead initiatives related to MBA admissions, alumni, career development and more to advocate for and empower the Latinx community both on and off-campus. Annual Events Fall and Spring Retreats Hispanic Heritage Month Celebration Prospective Student Days Diversity Career Fair Annual Alumni Dinner
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Latter-day Saint Student Association
description: The purpose of the LDSSA is to help LDS students remain close to Jesus Christ and grounded in His teachings while navigating the rigorous and fast-paced environment of Harvard Business School. The club supports students in balancing the demands of HBS with their personal, family, and church responsibilities. In addition, HBS LDSSA represents The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints within the HBS community and provides opportunities for friendship, fellowship, and networking—both among members and with the broader HBS community. Annual Events Weekly LDSSA Institute Speaker Series Winter Retreat New Admit Social
eligibility: Open to all matriculated HBS students and their registered partners

name: Latter-day Saints
description: The Harvard Law School Latter-day Saints (HLLDS) is made up of HLS students and their families who are members of, or interested in, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. HLLDS provides support for students seeking to maintain a spiritual foundation during their study of the law and allows members to associate with other students who have similar religious backgrounds and interests. HLLDS became an official chapter of the J. Reuben Clark Law Society in 2005.

name: Law & International Development Society
description: The Harvard Law School Law & International Development Society (LIDS) is the premier student-run organization at Harvard University focused on issues at the intersection of law, policy and international development. LIDS members are graduate students at Harvard Law School, the Kennedy School of Government, the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy, the Harvard School of Public Health, the Harvard Graduate School of Education, and other graduate schools in the Boston area.

name: Law & Political Economy Association
description: The Harvard Law School Law & Political Economy Association ( LPEA) is a student organization at Harvard Law School formed with the aim of promoting scholarship and teaching that investigates how legal practice has been central to the growth economic inequality and how legal tools may be repurposed to respond to this problem. The Group aims to bring questions of political economy to the center of law school life through activities such as a regular speaker series, workshops to develop alternative curricula, and to develop a cases-and-materials book that would act as a ready reference for a law-and-political economy canon.

name: Law & Technology Society
description: The Harvard Law School Law & Technology Society ( HLTS) is Harvard’s premier student organization for examining the way technology impacts the law. We use hackathons, collaborations with the Library Innovation Lab and independent research on legal tech law to probe the essential relationship between emerging technologies, legal practice and governance.

name: Middle Eastern & North African Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Middle Eastern Law Students Association (MELSA) is an affinity group created to serve and bring together Middle Eastern and North African students at Harvard Law. MELSA’s mission is threefold: (1) to build a cultural community amongst Middle Eastern and North African law students and alumni, (2) to further the professional and academic development of its members, and (3) to organize around political and legal issues that impact Middle Eastern and North African communities.

name: Midwest Student Association
description: Our goals are to create opportunities for Midwesterners and students interested in living in the Midwest post MBA to interact with each other, to increase awareness of the cultures and job opportunities available in the region, and to help employers from the Midwest match their recruiting needs with the job interests of Harvard Business School.
