name: Mignone Center for Career Success
description: The Mignone Center for Career Success (MCS) welcomes students from all Griffin GSAS departments and offers a wide range of services and resources tailored specifically to the needs of master's and Ph.D. students. MCS helps students prepare for today’s competitive job markets within the academy and beyond. We look forward to welcoming you. Free coffee and tea is always available in our main floor lounge.

name: Minority Biomedical Scientists Association of Harvard Griffin GSAS
description: Minority Biomedical Scientists Association of Harvard Griffin GSAS (MBSA of Harvard Griffin GSAS) is a graduate student group that aims to improve the experience of Harvard Griffin GSAS scientists from underrepresented backgrounds through community building and career development. Our main intent is to provide a welcoming and intellectually-enriching environment to support the diverse population of Harvard Griffin GSAS students. Fundamental to the vision of the organization is the belief that networking with faculty and alumni, developing camaraderie with peers, and celebrating individuality and inclusivity is paramount to the success of Harvard Griffin GSAS students. MBSA of Harvard Griffin GSAS seeks to foster this interaction by creating opportunities for Harvard Griffin GSAS students to learn from successful scientists of color in academic and non-academic careers alike. MBSA of Harvard Griffin GSAS also promotes these objectives through social and professional networking events that address the needs of our academic community and celebrates the diverse cultures and backgrounds of Harvard Griffin GSAS students. /p\r\npa title="MBSH Video" href="https://youtu.be/K7YxDhHB2AI"https://youtu.be/K7YxDhHB2AI/a/p

name: Mock Trial Association
description: The Harvard Law School Mock Trial Association ( HLSMTA) is a nationally recognized trial advocacy program that competes against other highly ranked law schools throughout the country in both civil and criminal cases. We hold tryouts each Fall, inviting everyone with an interest in trial advocacy. Whether you are a college mock trial veteran or new to the courtroom, we are excited to have you!

name: Muslim Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Muslim Law Students Association ( MLSA) is a student-run organization that serves Muslim law students by acting as a nexus of community-building, increasing awareness of issues that particularly impact Muslims, and building campus wide coalitions with other organizations dedicated to pluralism and meaningful discourse.

name: National Lawyers Guild
description: The Harvard Law School National Lawyers Guild ( NLG) is dedicated to the need for basic change in the structure of our political and economic system. It seeks to unite the lawyers, law students, legal workers and jailhouse lawyers to function as an effective force in the service of the people, to the end that human rights shall be regarded as more sacred than property interests.

name: National Security & Law Association
description: The Harvard Law School National Security & Law Association ( NSLA)’s only objective is to promote discourse on national security at Harvard Law School. The organization brings distinguished national security scholars and practitioners to campus for lunchtime lectures, assists members with career advice and networking opportunities, provides academic resources to the entire Harvard community, and produces high-quality reports on pressing national security matters.

name: National Society of Black Physicists Harvard Departmental Group
description: The National Society of Black Physicists (NSBP) Harvard Chapter Departmental Group is part of the larger joint Harvard-MIT NSBP Chapter. We seek to connect members through social engagement between both campuses. As the number of Black students in physics increases at both institutions, the need for a space to commune and share experiences becomes even more important. We seek to engage members through STEM outreach at local high schools and grade schools. We believe that connecting with students early on in their schooling can have a profound positive impact on their trajectories. We seek to enrich members through professional networking with faculty at both institutions and beyond. Building upon the experiences and perspectives of established scientists is necessary to foster innovation within our membership. Finally, we seek to cultivate members through research panels and scientific discussions. By exposing ourselves to feedback from a variety of fields and specialties, the critical thinking of our members will increase manyfold, enhancing research productivity.

name: Native American and Indigenous Health Organization (NAIHO) for HMS Students
Native American Law Students Association
description: The Harvard Law School Native American Law Students Association (NALSA) is a student-run organization dedicated to fostering a supportive atmosphere for Native American students at Harvard Law School, and is composed of Native American law students and students interested in issues affecting the Native community.

name: Natives at Harvard College
description: Our mission is to create social, intellectual, and cultural activities for both Indigenous/Native students at Harvard and for other interested members of the Harvard community. We recognize that Indigenous/Native students are an ultra-minority and attempt to foster a sense of community among our members. We also try to educate the Harvard community about Indigenous/Native issues and debunk popular misconceptions of Indigenous/Native individuals through our activities and events.

name: Omo Naija x Wahala Boys: Harvard Undergraduate African Dance Troupe
description: The mission of Omo Naija x The Wahala Boys is to educate the members of the greater Harvard community through dance and its role in the culture of the Afro-Caribbean. While dance is not generally imagined when one imagines education, the arts have historically served as some of the best cultural and educational tools available. While Omo Naija is close-knit, it is also a space for members of the African Diaspora across campus to find cultural roots, and to take part in the making and spreading of something amazing. Many on this campus know very little about Afro-Caribbean dance and culture and thus while we love that this organization is a fun way to express ourselves, it also serves as a community with which the Harvard community can engage, participate, and learn.

name: On Thin Ice
description: OTI commits to performing improv comedy at least once a month, free of charge and on Harvard’s campus.

name: Opportunities for Graduate Students

name: Orchestra - Student Center Fellows
description: Dedicated to the practice and performance of orchestral music at Harvard University and within the broader Cambridge community, the Student Center Orchestra is the community orchestra of Harvard’s Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School for Arts and Sciences. The Student Center Orchestra is composed primarily of Harvard graduate students, staff, and post-docs from across the university and aims to create and maintain a focused and inclusive environment to enjoy the experience of music-making. We welcome musicians of diverse musical backgrounds and a wide range of levels.

name: Organization of Asian American Sisters in Service
Organization of Harvard College Puerto Rican Students
description: The Organization of Harvard College Puerto Rican Students (LaO) seeks to promote Puerto Rican culture on campus and increase awareness of the current economic and social circumstances impacting the Carribean Island. Through various initiatives and events by LaO, Harvard undergraduates will learn more about Puerto Rico in an educational, impactful and enriching environment. In doing so, LaO seeks to foster a supportive community for Puerto Rican students on campus.

name: Orthodox Christian Fellowship of Harvard Undergraduates
description: To build community for Orthodox Christian students on campus!

name: Outdoors Club
description: The Outdoors Club provides opportunities, education, and community for adventurers at HBS. Whether you are an experienced outdoorsperson or a beginner weekend warrior, this club is for you! In addition to a great line-up of events, Outdoors Club also offers members discounts from top outdoor company partners, such as Hipcamp, Arc’teryx, and adidas Outdoor. Annual Events • Boston-area exploration opportunities • Day and overnight trips in the Northeast • Education and skills development sessions • International treks during winter and spring breaks • Social activities and mixers with other outdoors clubs in the city • Outdoor industry speaker events with top companies and athletes

The Club hopes to acclimate new partners to HBS life and broaden its members' experiences through a variety of events. Eligible members include spouses, boyfriends, girlfriends, fiances, and domestic partners. Through meaningful collaboration, we cultivate a space where learning thrives, curiosity is celebrated, and young minds are excited to question, explore, and lead.

name: Poker Equity Club
description: The mission of the Women's Poker Club is to empower HBS women by teaching the skills and strategies of poker in a fun, inclusive, and educational environment. We aim to increase the representation of women in the traditionally male-dominated game of poker and to help members develop valuable business skills such as decision-making under uncertainty, risk management, patience, discipline, and confidence. name: Portuguese Language Table Student Center
description: Welcome to the Portuguese Language Table! We are meeting every Monday throughout the semester to chat informally in Portuguese. It is a great opportunity to get to know other Portuguese learners, practice your Portuguese, and share with other peers your passion for the language and the culture from the Lusophony - the Portuguese-speaking countries and regions such as Angola, Brazil, and Portugal. Everyone from all levels, from beginners to native speakers, are welcome! Since we are a newly reactivated group, we can tailor our conversation topics to our interests, including language learning, culture, music, school, and traveling.

name: Presidential Initiative on Interfaith Engagement
description: The Presidential Initiative on Interfaith Engagement is committed to fostering pluralism and building a campus where respect for all identities flourishes, relationships between communities are built, and cooperation for the common good is a lived reality. We host programming across all of Harvard's campuses that bring students together across religious, spiritual, and ethical difference to build relationships and share about the guiding principles and practices that shape our lives.

name: PRIDE
description: Our Mission PRIDE, a Student Club at Harvard Business School, is an association of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and questioning (LGBTQ+) MBA students and partners. Together we work to build community, foster professional development, and encourage advocacy for LGBTQ+ representation at our school and in business. Our Vision We create a supportive environment for emerging leaders to socialize with one another, connect with employers seeking diverse talent, and engage in thought leadership in key areas of business and management. In partnership with our allies and alumni, we advocate for our members in conversations about diversity, equity, and inclusion in the wider HBS community. We believe that by promoting understanding of the queer experience, we will increase acceptance and advance our equality as business leaders. Annual Events 80s Party Club Retreat Diversity Career Fair LGBTQ+ Admissions Open House Reaching Out MBA (ROMBA) Conference National Coming Out Day Celebration World AIDS Day Love at HBS National Trans Day of Visibility Other club happy hours and events throughout the year! Club Membership PRIDE understands and respects that everyone has a different journey; our members are in control of their own narrative and we have different categories of membership to reflect that. PRIDE members can choose between three types of membership: Ambassador – Ambassador Members openly identify as LGBTQ+ or a partner of an LGBTQ+ PRIDE member to HBS and externally. Community – Community Members identify as LGBTQ+ or a partner of an LGBTQ+ PRIDE member to other members of PRIDE at HBS, but are confidential outside of the club. Informed – Informed Members identify as LGBTQ+ or a partner of an LGBTQ+ PRIDE member and receive our newsletter but wish to remain confidential to the club, HBS, and externally. Informed members are known only by the Co-Presidents, the Chief Operating Officer, the Communications Directors, and the Community Directors (6 club leaders total). For more information or to learn what this means practically, please reach out to pride@studentclubs.hbs.edu or either of the Co-Presidents and your message will be held in confidence. Otherwise, please feel free to reach out to either or both Co-Presidents listed below and your message will be held in confidence. Information For Recruiters For recruiters wishing to connect with PRIDE at HBS please reach out to pride@studentclubs.hbs.edu and your message will be forwarded to our club’s Careers team who will reach out with various ways to reach our club members. Information For Current MBA Students and Partners If you wish to join the club and missed us at the club fair, send an email to pride@studentclubs.hbs.edu or the Co-Presidents and we will be in touch! name: The Harvard Undergraduate Ichthus
description: The Harvard Ichthus is a journal of Christian thought. It exists for the purpose of fostering deep Christian thought among the members of the Harvard community, taking seriously the motto of Harvard University: “Veritas Christo et Ecclesiae,” in English “Truth for Christ and the Church.” It adopts these words of the Rev. Prof. Peter J. Gomes, preached at the Memorial Church, as its mission statement: "There is a rumor about, and fanned in certain quarters, that this University has long since abandoned its ancient motto and is conformable only to ‘Veritas.’ That simply is not true. The seal by which the President and Fellows of Harvard College continue to conduct their business is still the seal that says: ‘Veritas Christo et Ecclesiae.’ One cannot undo the past, and in this particular case one should not undo the past. The university-- and this University in particular-- is in the business of goodness and virtue personified, and not simply in the bottom lines of fairness and excellence. Christ and the Church were an essential part of that truth to which Harvard and the generations of its children were committed. ...Truth for Christ and the Church is not here by accident or by sufferance; it is here by design and intent. ...Indeed, as a symbol of Christian truth, we are here to remind Harvard of a dimension beyond its own self-interest and self-perception... We Christians must never forget, nor must we permit our College or our University ever to forget, that knowledge without virtue is a destructive danger that produces arrogant technocrats who are a danger to all that is holy, hopeful, lovely, and true, and who must be resisted. Our pious ancestors understood this, and thus they dedicated this small, fragile College in the wilderness to a truth that was seen in and for Christ and the Church. Veritas-- that is, true Veritas, and not simply correct information-- can never be separated from the one in whom it is most perfectly and fully seen: Jesus Christ. Not everyone may believe that, but those of us who do must not be intimidated by those who don't, and we must be emboldened to claim that truth not only as our own but as one that is essential to the definition of a University and College worthy of the name." (Strength for the Journey, pgs. 56, 60)
